raw.description:
We're unlocking access to the NHS, because healthcare is not truly free until it's truly accessible 💙

The world’s best healthcare, for free. It's not a new idea, it's called the NHS. But the largest healthcare provider is fundamentally broken. Patient satisfaction is at an all time low, and the biggest reason cited is lack of access. So we’re on a mission to fix it with technology that actually works.

We're building the front door of UK healthcare, creating a future where one billion NHS appointments are transparent and instantly bookable, and patients are guided to the right service first time using AI.

We're developing critical national infrastructure. Today, 26% of GP practices in England use our patient registration software, while one in five GP practices in London use Bookable Search to help new patients find and book appointments seamlessly.

Our latest product, Bookable Navigator, extends this vision by automatically booking appointments for existing patients.

We operate from within a working GP practice in East London 🏥 We're backed by Y Combinator, Innovate UK and the NHS Clinical Entrepreneur Programme, and were previously ranked the 8th fastest-growing startup in the UK and 33rd fastest-growing in Europe 🚀

⛩️ Our Principles

Exciting challenges lie ahead. Guided by our principles, we’ll meet these challenges with a thoughtful and caring approach. These principles drive everything we do at Healthtech-1:

  1. 💙 Care deeply

  2. 🏋️‍♀️ Work hard

  3. 🤝 Be your word

  4. 💬 Trust in radical truth and transparency

  5.  🚀 Do your life's best work

  6. 🥳 Find the fun

Read more about our principles and our "why" in the Healthtech-1 Handbook.

🎯 Goal expectations

As our Revenue Operations Manager, you’ll own the tooling and data that let’s Healthtech-1 scale across the NHS.

You’ll work closely across the GTM teams, deploy internal tooling with AI, turn Attio into our source of truth, and build an intelligent GTM motion on top.

This is an IC role, not a people management role. One week you might be rolling your sleeves up with the growth team, to be one or two steps ahead in identifying what the team need to hit their targets, and building internal tooling with AI to support the team. The next week you might be deep in the data, bringing company-wide data sources together to aide growth strategy planning e.g. identifying high demand areas in our marketplace, where we need to increase supply.

Objective 1: Keep systems and data running at a high standard

You will own and maintain Attio (our CRM), including its infrastructure, workflows and data hygiene across accounts and products. You will also own all our GTM tooling (e.g. Aircall, Calendly, Granola) and keep them running and improving. You will build a lot of tooling yourself using AI (e.g. dashboard, maps). You will run practice enrichment and data scraping pipelines so our data on customers stays current and usable.

Objective 2: Give the team and leadership clear visibility

You will build and maintain dashboards tracking company growth, cycle targets and product adoption. You will own reporting on practice numbers and growth trends. You will maintain tracking so leadership always has clear visibility on where deals are at.

Objective 3: Enable the growth team to sell more

The Growth team are your customer. You will build and maintain quality lead lists for AEs. You will support AEs with operational queries, targets and tooling. You will help new growth hires ramp faster through better tooling and playbooks.

Objective 4: Drive operational improvement

You will find and build automations and workflow improvements that save the team time. You will spot friction in how the growth team operates and fix it. You will actively look for ways to help the team drive more revenue.

⚠️ This role is not for everyone

This is a high-ownership, high-expectation role. You'll be working in a fast-moving healthtech environment where accuracy, speed, and proactivity all matter at the same time.

You probably won't enjoy this role if you:

  • Prefer to be told what to do over figuring out what to do

  • Treat ops as a support function rather than a growth lever

  • Aren't comfortable getting your hands dirty with data

  • Are content to maintain the status quo rather than improve it

  • Have never built things with AI

You will enjoy this role if you like owning systems end-to-end, building and deploying things with AI, and making the people around you more effective.

👍 Required experience

  • 2+ years in a revenue operations role in an early-stage startup, where you've owned systems, data and process improvement

  • Experience with Attio (or similar CRMs like HubSpot, Salesforce)

✅ Must-have traits

  • Great with AI - you know how to leverage AI well, whilst thoroughly checking accuracy

  • Detail oriented - you’re obsessed with the detail and CRM being the source of truth

  • Love data - you can build dashboards, spot trends, and make data useful for decision-making

  • Proactive problem solver - you don't wait for someone to flag a problem; you find it and fix it end-to-end.

  • Bias to action - you ship improvements quickly rather than over-planning

  • Team player - low ego, approachable and feedback-oriented; you get a kick from seeing the impact your work has on unlocking the sales team

  • Clear communicator - you keep stakeholders informed without being chased

💙 Desired traits

  • Comfortable with data scraping, enrichment tools and light automation (e.g. Zapier, Make, scripts)

  • Experience building dashboards and reports (e.g. Metabase, Looker, Google Sheets)

  • Familiarity with sales tooling (Calendly, Aircall, or equivalents)

  • Experience writing operational playbooks or onboarding materials

😊 The hiring process (4 stages)

  • 👋 Intro chat - with our Talent Partner, to learn more about each other

  • 📝 Take home task - complete a short task

  • 💼 An in-office work trial - work with the growth team on a real problem [1 day, fully paid]

  • ⛩️ Principles interview - with a Founder, to understand that our values align

  • 🎉 Offer!

💙 A bit about us

💙 We’re all NHS staff. We’re inside-outsiders. Trusted with one of the biggest datasets in the world.

🏥 Our office is within a GP practice. This is our unfair advantage. Got a question? Pop down the corridor. Want to learn how your work affects real patients? Pop downstairs to reception.

💪🏼 4 days in the office and 1 day WFH (for most roles). We highly prioritise in-person communication and prefer candidates who want to work 4+ days a week in the office. Our anchor days are Mon, Tues, Thurs and Fri. Homemade breakfast and lunch are on the house every day when you're in the office, ensuring you're fuelled for success!

🌀 We work in growth cycles. Every 8 weeks we do the same set of activities. 1 week outside of Business-as-Usual to research, strategise, plan our work. 7 weeks to knuckle down and deliver it.

🤝 We’re highly collaborative. One of the benefits of a high trust team is we often work autonomously, but as a team we’re very collaborative by nature. Two heads are often better than one, and we frequently lean on each other to solve problems together.

🤜🏽 We’re backed by industry leaders. We’re on the DigitalHealth.London Accelerator, backed by the NHS Clinical Entrepreneur Program, winners of the London Business School Healthtech Challenge, Innovate UK, and Y Combinator (S23).

🚀 An opportunity for real upside

💉 Paid volunteer days. We offer an additional 2 paid days off per year where you can give back to your mission of choice.

🎢 Every 8 weeks we take a day off to socialise as a team. In the past we’ve hiked box hill, raved at All Points East and spent one rainy day at Thorpe park. This works out as 6 working days a year.

📚 Learning budget of £250 annually and time off to spend it - we care about this; this is flexible and based on need but everyone will receive a yearly allocation towards their continual growth.

🍽️ Homemade breakfast and lunch are on the house when you're in the office, ensuring you're fuelled for success!

🥡 Team takeaways every Monday night

🥗 Health and fitness budget of £60 per month - see more here

🧘‍♂️ An additional 7 days of paid leave is available if you want to take time to learn how to meditate.

💫 Tooling; You’ll have your choice of operating systems and any additional tools you need to do your best work (e.g. keyboard, additional monitors, mouse etc). If you’re on our Engineering teams you’ll receive the latest MacBook Pro and our Growth & Ops teams receives a MacBook Air.

🩺 We know health and family come first which is why we have a generous sick leave policy with additional days that can be taken for mental health leave.

✈️ We prioritise time outside of work to bond, once a year we’ll holiday together! Destination chosen by popular vote. In 2025, we spent 8 days in a surf camp in France!

👎 No private medical insurance, because we believe in the NHS and we are here to improve it!

🐥 Parental leave: Post passing probation it is: statutory - 6 weeks 90% pay then, SMP for 33 weeks; if you've been an employee for a year: 12 weeks 100% pay then, SMP for 27 weeks; and if you have been here for 2 years: 18 weeks 100% pay then, SMP for 21 weeks. This will improve over time. We also include up to £9,000 of childcare contribution for primary caregivers to support a five-day return where possible.

👪 Fertility leave. We understand how difficult a fertility journey can be. This is why we give an extra 5 days off per year if you or your partner are going through fertility treatment.

🐖 Pension - We operate a standard 3% employer contribution and employees auto-contribute 5% of their salary. We use Nest as our provider.

🏡 Local living benefit - A one-off benefit to support living closer to the office: £5,000 if you live within a 30-minute walk, or £2,500 within a 30-minute bike. It is optional, available immediately on signing, and not linked to performance or progression.

🚕 If you choose to work late in the office, you can expense dinner after 7pm and an Uber home after 9pm, or earlier if you feel unsafe travelling in the dark. This is optional and about wellbeing, not performance or expectations.

⛵️And of course, an adventure of a lifetime!

🌈 Inclusive & Diverse by Design

We care about building a product that is loved and a culture that is rich in perspectives, experiences, and backgrounds.

Our team represents more than ten different cultures. We come together every lunch time for a home cooked meal, rotated among team members!

We want everyone in our team to know that they belong. We are purposeful about this and are proactively building a company that is inclusive of all people; from race, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, neurodiversity, disability, colour, and national origin - essentially every type of diversity. We don’t just want people who fit in, we want them to fit together. We're active in continually improving the way we make this happen.

raw.title: Commissioning & Field Deployment Engineer
raw.description:
At Hive, we're building the defining physical AI platform of the next decade.

Industrial labor is one of the most acute bottlenecks in the global economy. Operators are expensive, hard to retain, and working in environments that are increasingly unsafe. The shortage is structural. The window to solve it is now.

Our answer is a machine-agnostic intelligence platform that lets any machine, on any site, perceive, decide, and act autonomously. One platform. Any machine. No fleet replacement.

Already live across multiple sites and customers in Europe - spanning logistics and warehousing, industrial manufacturing, and large-scale chemical production - with a US expansion underway.

The vision: one operator managing hundreds of machines simultaneously. Productive machine-hour cost dropping by 80x, and unlocks the next productivity revolution in physical work.

The mission is to make productivity limitless. Come and help us build it.

 

The Role

As Commissioning & Field Deployment Engineer, you will be responsible for the hands-on installation, integration, testing and commissioning of Hive systems, mainly at customer sites.

You will work directly on industrial machines alongside Hive Engineering and Delivery, taking systems from physical installation through technical commissioning and operational readiness.

This is a field-focused engineering role for someone comfortable combining mechanical, electrical and software-based troubleshooting in real industrial environments.

What You Will Do

Install & Integrate Hive Systems

  • Perform mechanical and electrical installation of Hive equipment on industrial machines.

  • Install, connect and verify system hardware and related components.

  • Build, modify and troubleshoot wiring, harnesses, brackets and installation components when required.

  • Verify installations against drawings, specifications and quality requirements.

  • Prepare machines and equipment for commissioning and deployment.

Commission Systems

  • Perform system configuration, calibration and commissioning.

  • Execute commissioning procedures, functional testing and technical verification.

  • Verify that system components and machine interfaces operate correctly.

  • Diagnose and resolve installation, configuration and commissioning issues.

  • Document commissioning results, issues and corrective actions.

  • Support final validation and readiness for customer operation.

Support Customer Deployments

  • Travel to customer sites across the UK to install and commission Hive solutions.

  • Work closely with the Deployment Manager, Engineering and customer teams during deployment.

  • Troubleshoot technical issues in active industrial environments.

  • Support testing, validation, acceptance and go-live activities.

  • Provide hands-on technical support during the early stages of customer operations.

Improve How We Deploy

  • Improve installation and commissioning procedures based on field experience.

  • Identify recurring issues and feed practical improvements back to Engineering.

  • Help develop tools, documentation and checklists for future deployments.

  • Support preparation of machines and equipment at Hive's UK facility.

  • Help establish a high standard for installation quality, commissioning and field execution.

What We're Looking For

Essential

  • Hands-on experience with mechanical, electrical or electromechanical systems.

  • Experience installing, commissioning, maintaining or troubleshooting industrial equipment.

  • Strong practical troubleshooting skills.

  • Comfortable reading technical drawings, wiring diagrams and installation documentation.

  • Experience working with electrical wiring, sensors, control systems or industrial electronics.

  • Comfortable using computers and software-based diagnostic or configuration tools.

  • Strong attention to quality and safety.

  • Able to work independently and solve problems in the field.

  • Comfortable working directly with customers and other technical teams.

  • Willingness to travel extensively across the UK.

  • Authorized to work in the UK.

Strongly preferred

Experience with one or more of:

  • Industrial automation

  • Robotics or autonomous systems

  • Heavy equipment

  • Forklifts or material-handling equipment

  • Construction or mining machinery

  • Automotive or off-highway equipment

  • Field service engineering

  • Controls or electrical systems

  • Sensor installation and calibration

  • Linux-based systems

  • Industrial networking

Experience commissioning complex systems in customer environments is a major advantage.

Who Thrives at Hive

  • You prefer working on real machines over sitting behind a desk.

  • You enjoy figuring out why something doesn't work — and fixing it.

  • You are comfortable combining mechanical, electrical and software troubleshooting.

  • You take pride in clean, reliable installations and high-quality field work.

  • You work well in fast-moving environments where not every problem has a documented solution.

  • You want to help build a field engineering capability from the ground up.

This is an opportunity to play a direct role in bringing Hive's technology from engineering into real industrial operations across the UK.

Why Join Hive?

Join Hive at a pivotal stage as we expand into the UK and build a new category in Physical AI. You’ll work with cutting-edge autonomy technology and a highly experienced team to bring autonomous industrial machines out of development and into real-world commercial operations.

As we establish and scale our UK operations, you’ll have the opportunity to take on significant responsibility from day one, help shape how we operate in the UK, and build the playbooks for deploying and operating autonomous machines at scale..

Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis, and the position may be filled before the application deadline. Early applications are encouraged. Hive values diversity and encourages qualified candidates to apply regardless of gender, age, ethnicity, religion, disability, sexual orientation or background.

The mission is to make productivity limitless. Come and help us build it.

 

The Role

As Commissioning & Field Deployment Engineer, you will be responsible for the hands-on installation, integration, testing and commissioning of Hive systems, mainly at customer sites.

You will work directly on industrial machines alongside Hive Engineering and Delivery, taking systems from physical installation through technical commissioning and operational readiness.

This is a field-focused engineering role for someone comfortable combining mechanical, electrical and software-based troubleshooting in real industrial environments.

What You Will Do

Install & Integrate Hive Systems

  • Perform mechanical and electrical installation of Hive equipment on industrial machines.

  • Install, connect and verify system hardware and related components.

  • Build, modify and troubleshoot wiring, harnesses, brackets and installation components when required.

  • Verify installations against drawings, specifications and quality requirements.

  • Prepare machines and equipment for commissioning and deployment.

Commission Systems

  • Perform system configuration, calibration and commissioning.

  • Execute commissioning procedures, functional testing and technical verification.

  • Verify that system components and machine interfaces operate correctly.

  • Diagnose and resolve installation, configuration and commissioning issues.

  • Document commissioning results, issues and corrective actions.

  • Support final validation and readiness for customer operation.

Support Customer Deployments

  • Travel to customer sites across the UK to install and commission Hive solutions.

  • Work closely with the Deployment Manager, Engineering and customer teams during deployment.

  • Troubleshoot technical issues in active industrial environments.

  • Support testing, validation, acceptance and go-live activities.

  • Provide hands-on technical support during the early stages of customer operations.

Improve How We Deploy

  • Improve installation and commissioning procedures based on field experience.

  • Identify recurring issues and feed practical improvements back to Engineering.

  • Support preparation of machines and equipment at Hive's UK facility.

  • Help establish a high standard for installation quality, commissioning and field execution.

What We're Looking For

Essential

  • Automotive or off-highway equipment

  • Sensor installation and calibration

  • Linux-based systems

  • Industrial networking

raw.description:
The Account Manager (AM) is a key client partner and collaborative leader within Infinite Lambda. Responsible for owning and growing accounts, AMs play a crucial role in ensuring successful delivery, maintaining client satisfaction, and driving commercial outcomes. While AMs are expected to operate independently, they collaborate closely with delivery teams and seek support from Senior Account Managers when needed.

This role belongs to the Account Management Department, part of the broader Customer Success Division. AMs work cross-functionally with Engineering Excellence and Delivery Excellence teams, ensuring alignment between client goals and internal execution.

This role does not include direct reports but requires strong leadership through influence. You will collaborate with engineers, architects, analysts, project managers, and commercial teams to deliver measurable client outcomes and drive revenue growth.

Key Objectives

  • Drive sustainable, forecastable growth: Secure new business opportunities from assigned accounts, retain clients, and ensure their satisfaction through exceptional delivery.

  • Build enduring partnerships: Establish yourself as a trusted partner to clients, ensuring long-term collaboration and profitability.

You lead by example and foster a culture based on trust, empowerment, and excellence with your accounts and the teams you work with.

 

Detailed Responsibilities

Client Relationship Management

  • Develop and nurture strong relationships with assigned clients, serving as the main point of contact and advocate for their needs;

  • Understand each client’s business objectives, challenges, and strategic goals to deliver tailored solutions that align with their vision;

  • Proactively establish Infinite Lambda as a trusted partner, consistently delivering tangible value and maintain client engagement ;

  • Facilitate regular check-ins, quarterly business reviews, and strategic planning sessions to ensure alignment and promote long-term partnerships.

  • Act as a cultural ambassador, fostering trust-based relationships that reflect Infinite Lambda’s values and create a positive, lasting experience for both clients and colleagues;

  • Champion sustainable growth by aligning client success with long-term partnership and responsible use of data and AI technology.

Revenue Growth & Account Development

  • Identify upselling and cross-selling opportunities within client environments;

  • Drive renewals and contract discussions, with support from commercial leadership as needed;

  • Drive financial performance by meeting revenue targets, securing competitive pricing, and maintaining consistent growth in gross margins and profitability;

  • Proactively manage opportunity pipelines, converting opportunities into measurable revenue.

Strategic Account Planning

  • Define and implement account strategies in line with the direction provided by the Chief Customer Success Officer (CCO);

  • Collaborate with sales, marketing, and delivery teams to develop comprehensive account strategies that leverage Infinite Lambda’s offerings and expertise;

  • Analyse client industries, competitors, and market trends to identify growth opportunities and mitigate risks;

  • Contribute insights to product and service development based on client feedback and market needs.

 

Sales Handover & Onboarding

  • Take ownership of new accounts after contract signature;

  • Lead smooth client onboarding processes in coordination with delivery and sales.

 

Collaboration & Internal Alignment

  • Coordinate with project teams to ensure alignment on client deliverables, project timelines, and resource allocation;

  • Work closely with project teams to identify opportunities for innovation or new initiatives within accounts;

  • Act as the primary escalation point for client-related issues, ensuring swift and effective resolution while preserving relationships;

  • Provide regular updates and insights to internal stakeholders, ensuring company-wide visibility on account health and performance.

Operational Excellence

  • Maintain high standards across account efficiency, revenue performance, and client experience;

  • Track KPIs: revenue growth, NPS, forecast accuracy, GSS/FSS;

  • Produce at least two domain-relevant artefacts per year (e.g. case studies, blogs, market insights).

 

Compensation and Performance Targets

The compensation for the Account Manager role is composed of a base salary and a variable component tied directly to performance. The variable portion is determined by success in three key performance indicators (KPIs):

  • Financial Accuracy & Stability: Ensuring accounts are managed with precision, budgets are adhered to, and financial processes are stable and reliable;

  • Net Promoter Score (NPS): Driving client satisfaction and advocacy, as measured by their likelihood to recommend our services;

  • Account Revenue Growth and Sustain: Strategically fostering account growth through innovative solutions and long-term revenue stability.

This structure aligns rewards with results, ensuring performance excellence is recognised and incentivised.

 

Measurement Metrics

The success of the Account Manager role is evaluated based on the following categories:

 

Client Satisfaction

  • Client Feedback (NPS): Track satisfaction trends quarterly, ensuring consistent improvement from the baseline;

  • Referrals & Testimonials: Secure at least one public recommendation or referral per client.

Revenue Growth

  • Upselling/Cross-selling Revenue

  • Revenue Target Achievement

  • Gross Margin

  • Growth and Sustain Score (GSS)

  • Financial Stability Score (FSS)

Activity & Productivity

  • Client Interactions: Maintain consistent touchpoints through regular meetings and planning sessions.

  • Forecast Accuracy: Minimise the variance between initial forecasts and actual revenue.

 

Qualifications and Skills

  • Proven extensive experience in account management, client relationship development, and revenue growth;

  • Strong ability to build inclusive, trusted relationships with business and operational stakeholders, grow toward engaging executive leadership, and create positive experiences;

  • Strong consultative skills, with the ability to identify and address client needs proactively;

  • Excellent problem-solving skills with a results-driven mindset;

  • Outstanding communication, negotiation, and presentation skills;

  • Proficiency in analysing financial metrics and delivering data-driven insights;

  • Demonstrated ability to manage multi-year accounts in a dynamic environment;

  • High level of autonomy and capability to work with minimal oversight while delivering measurable results;

  • Exceptional collaboration and alignment skills, ensuring seamless interaction between clients and internal teams;

  • Commitment to supporting sustainable growth.

▶ ▶ Submit your CV in English in PDF.

Glance, which is pioneering new models of agentic commerce, is owned and operated by Glance InMobi Pte. Ltd., a non-consolidated subsidiary of InMobi Pte. Ltd.

InMobi Advertising

InMobi Advertising, part of global technology company InMobi, is an agentic advertising platform helping brands and merchants achieve their business outcomes. Through its proprietary intelligence, AI-led solutions, and vast consumer reach — including flagship consumer platform Glance — InMobi Advertising delivers the omnichannel performance defining what's next in advertising and commerce. Glance is owned and operated by Glance InMobi Pte. Ltd., a non-consolidated subsidiary of InMobi Pte. Ltd. To learn more, visit advertising.inmobi.com.

Glance

Glance is an intelligent shopping agent, redefining the commerce experience. Powered by proprietary agentic intelligence and generative AI, Glance delivers a hyper-personalized consumer experience across mobile and TV — shaping the new era of shopping. Glance is operated by Glance InMobi Pte. Ltd., a non-consolidated subsidiary of global technology leader InMobi, and is backed by Mithril Capital, Google and Jio Platforms. To learn more, visit glance.com.

Overview of the Role:

The Enterprise Gaming Partnerships team is part of InMobi's Supply organization and drives strategic growth across our advertising exchange. The team manages direct relationships with the world's leading mobile game developers and app publishers. It helps them get the most from their ad monetization through in-app bidding, mediation integrations, and high-quality global demand.

The role is based in London and is externally-facing. You'll build and grow partnerships with top-tier gaming and app publishers, with a focus on in-app formats such as rewarded video, interstitial, banner, and native. You'll also help publishers grow their user base by connecting them to InMobi's user acquisition (UA) solutions. Internally, you'll be the link between the publisher ecosystem and InMobi's Product, Demand, Marketplace, and Ad Quality teams, keeping everyone aligned so that partners get results.

Reporting to the Director of Enterprise Gaming, you'll own a book of business across EMEA, shape growth strategy for each partner, and represent InMobi at the major gaming and app industry events. You'll play a central part in strengthening InMobi's position as a leading monetization partner for gaming and apps.

The Impact You'll Make:

  • Represent and manage a portfolio of high-priority gaming and app publishers. Find growth opportunities, manage risks, and build plans that run across several quarters.
  • Take ownership of a defined book of strategic publisher accounts within your first 90 days.
  • Build strong relationships with studios. Learn their monetization stack, game economies, ad formats, and retention goals well enough to spot new opportunities and act on them.
  • Meet or exceed revenue targets every quarter while giving partners an outstanding experience.
  • Grow share of wallet within partners' mediation setups (AppLovin MAX, Google AdMob/Open Bidding, and Unity LevelPlay). Do this through bidding integrations, new placements, format expansion, and better performance.
  • Track key health metrics such as fill rate, eCPM, revenue per daily active user (ARPDAU), ad quality, and margin. Diagnose problems and work with internal teams to fix them.
  • Find cross-sell opportunities: help publishers grow their player base through InMobi's UA offering, and open brand demand for their inventory.
  • Work with Product, Demand, and Marketplace teams to line up supply and demand strategies, including new ad products and direct deals for gaming inventory.
  • Run enablement between publisher partners and internal Sales teams, so that buyers understand the value of gaming audiences and partners adopt new features.
  • Attend key industry events such as Pocket Gamer Connects, Gamesforum, MAU, GDC and Gamescom, and represent InMobi credibly in the gaming ecosystem.
  • Deepen your working technical knowledge of SDK integration, in-app bidding, mediation waterfalls, and how an SSP works.
  • Coach peers to raise the team's capabilities and contribute to the wider team's success.
  • Build growth plans with Business Development, Marketplace, Product, and Engineering, using publisher feedback to shape goals and the product roadmap.

The Experience We Need:

  • A flexible, startup mindset, a strong sense of ownership, and a track record of success in fast-paced, high-growth environments.
  • A proven ability to build, grow, and sell into customer relationships, ideally with existing accounts at mobile gaming or app companies.
  • Success in building account growth plans, influencing decision-makers, and agreeing on shared goals.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills. You can draw insight from monetization data, A/B tests, and performance dashboards, and you work well with ambiguity.
  • Experience managing multiple priorities with solid process and project management.
  • Proactive and action-oriented, and comfortable working across functions and time zones.
  • An established network across the EMEA mobile gaming ecosystem, including hubs such as London, Paris, Istanbul, Helsinki, Barcelona, Berlin, and Tel Aviv, and the confidence to meet partners in person at industry events.
  • Hands-on knowledge of in-app monetization: mediation platforms, in-app bidding, ad networks, and SSPs. Experience with UA or performance marketing is a plus.
  • Readiness to learn new systems and keep up with market trends such as privacy changes and mediation dynamics.
  • A collaborative team player with strong interpersonal skills, leadership instincts, and a sense of humor.

At InMobi, you'll be surrounded by people who…

  • Think big and act fast: We're entrepreneurial, thrive in ambiguity, and love solving high-impact problems
  • Are passionate, fanatically driven, and take immense pride in their work: We care deeply about the impact we create and continuously push our potential
  • Own their outcomes: We take responsibility, make bold decisions, and execute with confidence
  • Embrace freedom with accountability: We value autonomy and understand that trust comes with responsibility
  • Believe in lifelong learning: We welcome feedback, challenge ourselves to grow, and aren't afraid to take smart risks

Award-winning culture, best-in-class benefits

Our compensation philosophy enables us to provide a competitive salary that drives high performance while balancing business needs and pay parity. We determine compensation based on a wide variety of factors, including role, nature of experience, skills, and location.

For this role, an InMobian may also receive variable pay in the form of an annual variable bonus or quarterly variable bonus/sales incentive, as deemed per policy, in addition to fixed compensation.

In addition to cash compensation, based on the position, an InMobian can receive equity in the form of ESOPs (Employee Stock Option Plan). We believe that our employees/personnel should have the ability to own a part of the entity they are a part of. Therefore, the entity employing you may elect to provide such stock to you. Ownership of stock enables us to treat our employer company as our own and base our decisions on the company's best interests. To encourage a spirit of shared ownership, we grant InMobians relevant company stock(s). As you contribute to the growth of your company, certain stocks may be issued to you in recognition of your contribution.

If this sounds like the kind of team, role, values, benefits, and challenges that excite you, we'd love to hear from you!

InMobi is an equal opportunity employer
InMobi is a place where everyone can grow. Howsoever you identify, and whatever background you bring with you, we invite you to apply if this sounds like a role that would make you excited to work.

InMobi provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local laws. This policy applies to all terms and conditions of employment, including recruiting, hiring, placement, promotion, termination, layoff, recall, transfer, leaves of absence, compensation, and training.

The InMobi Culture

At InMobi, culture isn't a buzzword; it's an ethos woven by every InMobian, reflecting our diverse backgrounds and experiences.

We thrive on challenges and seize every opportunity for growth. Our core values — thinking big, being passionate, showing accountability, and taking ownership with freedom — guide us in every decision we make.

We believe in nurturing and investing in your development through continuous learning and career progression with our InMobi Live Your Potential program.

InMobi is proud to be an Equal Employment Opportunity employer and is committed to providing reasonable accommodations to qualified individuals with disabilities throughout the hiring process and in the workplace.

Visit https://www.inmobi.com/company/careers to better understand our benefits, values, and more!

Applied AI Engineer - Direct Acquisition
raw.description:
Applied AI Engineer - Direct Acquisition

We're planning this as a six-month secondment. There may be an opportunity to extend it or make it permanent.

We're looking for an Applied AI Engineer to join the Direct Acquisition team.

You'll design and build AI agents that run whole business processes, from planning the work to learning from the results. What you find will steer how far iwoca takes agents across the business.

The company

Small businesses move fast. Opportunities often don't wait, and cash flow pressures can appear overnight. To keep going, and growing, SMEs need finance that's as flexible and responsive as they are.

That's why we built iwoca. Our smart technology, data science and five-star customer service ensures business owners can act with the speed, confidence and control they need, exactly when it's needed.

We've already cleared the way for 100,000 businesses with more than £5 billion in funding. Our passionate team is driven to help even more SMEs succeed, through access to better finance and other services that make running a business easier. Our ultimate mission is to support one million SMEs in their defining moments, creating lasting impact for the communities and economies they drive.

The team

Direct Acquisition includes iwoca's Marketing, Sales, Brand and Acquisition Tech teams. Together, they reach UK businesses of all shapes and sizes through paid and organic marketing channels and direct sales.

A new team in Direct Acquisition builds agents that automate and improve acquisition processes. That's its only focus, and it works closely with Acquisition Tech. It's small – a product owner and you – and everyone builds. You'll report to the Head of Direct Acquisition, who sets the commercial direction.

The role

As the Applied AI Engineer, you'll build the agents and the systems around them. Most of the work is system design and backend engineering.

You'll start with direct mail. The first goal is an agent that plans each monthly round, uses iwoca's existing predictive models to build the mailing file, and learns from the results as they come in. The pattern is simple to say and hard to get right: the agent orchestrates, deterministic code does the work, and a human in the loop approves the file before it goes to print. You'll work with the people who run each process to understand the edge cases, and with Core Systems and Compliance on access and controls.

The agents don't exist yet, and much is still open: which processes the team takes on, and what the architecture looks like. You'll own those design decisions and write most of the code yourself, much of it with AI coding tools. Some of this won't work, and finding out why is one of the main outputs of the role.

  • Architecture. You'll design what agents need to run reliably: memory that persists between runs, task management, access to tools, permissions, and a record of every decision and why. You'll build each piece so the next process can reuse it.

  • Guardrails. You'll decide where the agent uses judgement and where code enforces rules the agent can't change, like suppressions, compliance checks and budget limits.

  • Delivery. You'll own each agent end to end: connect it to iwoca's predictive models, data pipelines and channel tools, and run it alongside the current process until it has shown it works.

  • Measurement. You'll track how often agents need a person, where they fail, what they cost, and what they're worth.

The requirements

We're looking for the depth of someone who has solved hard problems, and the pace of someone who moves fast in areas that are new to them.

Essential:

  • System ownership. You've owned a complex system end to end, from design to running it in production, and lived with the consequences of your architecture choices.

  • Design judgement. You've made architecture decisions other people built on, and you can explain the trade-offs and what you'd change. When an idea won't work, you say so and offer a better one.

  • Pace. You've got things live quickly in unfamiliar areas and they kept working once people relied on them.

  • Agent engineering. You've built systems where LLMs take actions – more than chat or summaries – and you can explain what went wrong and how you fixed it. You know when a problem needs an agent and when it needs a for-loop.

  • Controls. You've built permissions, data access rules and audit trails into systems from the start.

  • Constructive challenge. You work well with commercial and product colleagues, and when an idea won't work, you say so and offer a better one.

  • AI leverage. You've used AI coding tools to produce engineering work you couldn't have delivered without them – a service, an integration, or an internal tool others use. You have opinions on how to get the most out of them, and you check their output before it reaches production.

  • Communication. You write and speak clearly, directly, and concisely. You adapt technical detail to your audience.

Bonus:

  • Languages and data tools. You've worked with Python, Go, Snowflake or dbt.

  • Evaluation. You've built evals that measure how an agent performs and where it fails.

  • Marketing and growth tech. You've worked with ad platforms, CRMs or direct mail.

  • Quantitative foundations. You come from a numerical or technical field, such as physics, engineering, maths or computer science.

The culture

At iwoca, the best idea wins. We model our culture on independent thinking, challenging untested logic, and evidence-based decisions. We prioritise learning and growth, and give people the autonomy to develop in the direction that makes them most effective.

We're a tech company and believe in the power of AI to help us work faster and better. We provide the infrastructure where every iwocan always has access to the best models and where those models have access to all of our data. We will help our people to learn how to use and grow with the new tools available to them.

The offices

We put a lot of effort into making iwoca a great place to work:

  • Offices in London, Leeds, Berlin, and Frankfurt with plenty of drinks and snacks.

  • Events and community-led groups, including running groups, padel, and monthly ping-pong and pool competitions.

The benefits

  • Flexible working hours.

  • Medical insurance from Vitality, including discounted gym membership.

  • A private GP service (separate from Vitality) for you, your partner, and your dependents.

  • 25 days' holiday per year, an extra day off for your birthday, the option to buy or sell an additional five days of annual leave, and unlimited unpaid leave.

  • A one-month, fully paid sabbatical after four years.

  • Instant access to external counselling and therapy sessions for team members that need emotional or mental health support.

  • 3% Pension contributions on total earnings.

  • An employee equity incentive scheme.

  • Generous parental leave and a nursery tax benefit scheme to help you save money.

  • Electric car scheme and cycle to work scheme.

  • Two company retreats a year: we've been to France, Italy, Spain, and further afield.

And to make sure we all keep learning, we offer:

  • A learning and development budget for everyone.

  • Company-wide talks with internal and external speakers.

  • Access to learning platforms like Treehouse.

  • iwoca benefits & policies

Data Scientist - Broker Terms Team

Hybrid in London, United Kingdom

We're looking for a Data Scientist to join the Broker Terms team.

You'll shape the analytical approach for a team that sets the terms on iwoca's biggest acquisition channel. The team is young, with many unexplored opportunities.

The company

Small businesses move fast. Opportunities often don’t wait, and cash flow pressures can appear overnight. To keep going, and growing, SMEs need finance that’s as flexible and responsive as they are.

That's why we built iwoca. Our smart technology, data science and five-star customer service ensures business owners can act with the speed, confidence and control they need, exactly when it's needed.

We’ve already cleared the way for 100,000 businesses with more than £4 billion in funding. Our passionate team is driven to help even more SMEs succeed, through access to better finance and other services that make running a business easier. Our ultimate mission is to support one million SMEs in their defining moments, creating lasting impact for the communities and economies they ildrive.

The team

Broker Terms is a growing team that sits within iwoca's third-party acquisition department. It owns the full offer terms strategy for customers referred through the broker network – both first-time customers and repeat. The team sets pricing, loan amounts, durations, and broker commissions, and owns the UX that presents them to brokers and customers.

The team is small and interdisciplinary, combining commercial strategy, engineering, and data science. The work translates business questions into quantitative problems, and findings into actionable decisions. Active projects include:

  • Model-based pricing – creating a sophisticated model to offer bespoke pricing to each customer

  • A no-fee test – examining how our product performs when we remove all drawdown fees, and how that influence customer repayment behaviour

  • Testing longer-duration flexi-loan products with particular customer segments.

  • Reintroductions - exploring the right offer terms to give returning customers

The team is small and cross-functional – commercial strategy, engineering, design, and data science – and works across the full application stack, from the Broker API to the Introducer Portal brokers use.

The role

You'll model expected customer take-up rates, design experiments, and translate findings into pricing and product decisions for the acquisition channel that drives the most customer lifetime value (CLTV). Because the Broker Terms team is a young team, you'll influence how its analytical approach develops, not just what it produces.

The work has direct commercial consequences: brokers act on what the team builds and tests, and that shapes which customers iwoca wins and on what terms.

  • Offer terms and experimentation. You'll model how customers respond to offer terms and how brokers make decisions under uncertainty. You'll design experiments where causal inference is central: you'll need to know where standard A/B testing breaks down and what to reach for instead.

  • Commercial translation. You'll work with commercial and strategy colleagues and see your analysis applied directly in day-to-day decisions. That includes meeting brokers in person – gaining context that shapes how you frame and interpret results – and coordinating with adjacent teams responsible for underwriting decisions, repeat lending, and offer construction.

  • CLTV and customer journey. You'll think across the full broker-referred customer journey – from first funding to repeat – identifying what drives CLTV and what changes to offer terms or UX improve it. You own both the strategy and the mechanism, so your findings feed directly into what the team builds and tests.

  • AI and ways of working. You'll use AI to accelerate and automate your analytical work – not occasionally, but as a default. You should have a view on where it genuinely helps and where a different approach is better.

The requirements

Essential:

  • Statistical foundations. You have a background in probability and statistics from a quantitative field such as mathematics, physics, or statistics. You're comfortable with Bayesian reasoning, and have applied hierarchical models or formal decision-making under uncertainty in real work.

  • Causal inference and experimentation. You've separated signal from noise in observational and experimental data. You know where A/B testing breaks down and what to reach for instead. You have experience with careful experimental design to facilitate clean, trustworthy results.

  • Analytical ownership. You take loosely defined problems from start to finish – framing the question, choosing the method, and landing the answer with the people who act on it.

  • Data tooling. You're proficient with data manipulation and modelling tools, and with scientific computing libraries (pandas, numpy, sklearn, PyMC).

  • AI leverage. You've used AI to produce work you couldn't have delivered without it – an analysis pipeline, a prototype, or a tool others use. You judge where it helps and where it doesn't, and you check its output before anyone acts on it.

  • Communication. You write and speak clearly, directly, and concisely. You adapt technical detail for non-technical colleagues in commercial and strategy roles.

Bonus:

  • Modelling depth. You've built or adapted statistical or ML models and can explain the maths behind them to commercial stakeholders.

  • Stochastic methods. You've used stochastic processes for inference or time-series modelling.

  • Broker market insight. You've worked with brokers or other intermediaries in lending or financial services.

We're a tech company and believe in the power of AI to help us work faster and better. We provide the infrastructure where every iwocan always has access to the best models and where those models have access to all of our data. We will help our people to learn how to use and grow with the new tools available to them.

  • Offices in London, Leeds, Berlin, and Frankfurt with plenty of drinks and snacks.

  • Events and community-led groups, including running groups, padel, and monthly ping-pong and pool competitions.

The benefits

  • Flexible working hours.

  • Medical insurance from Vitality, including discounted gym membership.

  • A private GP service (separate from Vitality) for you, your partner, and your dependents.

  • 25 days’ holiday per year, an extra day off for your birthday, the option to buy or sell an additional five days of annual leave, and unlimited unpaid leave.

You’re joining manda, iwoca’s M&A platform, at a pivotal moment. After early success working with existing iwoca customers, we’re now turning to the open market to help more business owners exit.

That’s why we’re looking for a Growth Associate to join the team. This is a 6-month fixed-term role for someone smart, hungry and entrepreneurial. With the right traction the role will convert into a permanent role at the forefront of manda’s growth efforts.

The company

Selling a small business is hard. Only one in five UK SME owners has a formal exit plan, yet half are counting on their business to fund their retirement. Below £10m in enterprise value, most M&A advisers can't make the economics work, so a generation of owner-managers is getting ready to step back with no realistic route to a sale.

manda exists to fix that. We match owners with serious buyers, from search funds to private equity, and handle the whole process in one place, including financial due diligence and acquisition finance. Our first sale is done, and we're now opening manda up beyond iwoca's own customers.

manda is part of iwoca, one of Europe's leading fintech lenders, which has provided more than £4 billion in funding to over 150,000 businesses since 2012. That gives us what a traditional adviser doesn't have: a deep footprint in the SME economy, a lender's data and infrastructure, and deals run on clean, automated processes rather than spreadsheets.

You'll report to manda's Venture Lead and work day to day with our Transaction Managers, the dealmakers who run each sale, and our Partnerships Manager, who builds our referral network with accountants, solicitors and wealth managers. You'll also work with iwoca's marketing & sales team and have access to their tools and know-how.

  • Find what works. Run several experiments at once, back what produces meetings and drop what doesn't. Letters, events and ideas of your own can all earn a place.

  • You follow through. A reply that never becomes a meeting is a lead lost.

  • A genuine interest in SMEs, M&A or how businesses change hands.

At the end of the six months, we'll review how things have gone, with the opportunity to make the role permanent, expand its responsibilities and revisit the salary to reflect the longer-term scope.

Please include your salary expectations with your application.

Senior Data Scientist - Credit Risk Modelling

Hybrid in London or remote in the UK

We’re looking for a Senior Data Scientist to join our Credit Risk Modelling team.

You'll shape how iwoca models credit risk – setting the technical direction on multi-quarter projects, and lifting the bar for the team as you go.

The company

Small businesses move fast. Opportunities often don’t wait, and cash flow pressures can appear overnight. To keep going, and growing, SMEs need finance that’s as flexible and responsive as they are.

That's why we built iwoca. Our smart technology, data science and five-star customer service ensures business owners can act with the speed, confidence and control they need, exactly when it's needed.

We’ve already cleared the way for 100,000 businesses with more than £4 billion in funding. Our passionate team is driven to help even more SMEs succeed, through access to better finance and other services that make running a business easier. Our ultimate mission is to support one million SMEs in their defining moments, creating lasting impact for the communities and economies they drive.

The team

The Credit Risk Modelling team owns credit risk and Customer Lifetime Value (CLtV) modelling for iwoca's UK and German lending. That covers the probabilistic machine learning models behind every credit decision, plus the CLtV models that shape pricing and portfolio strategy.

The team is around twelve data scientists. Some work on auto-space models that decide within five minutes from data candidates authorise us to pull. Others work on manual-space models that pick up when a credit analyst adds digital footprint and income data, which lands a decision within 24 hours.

The role

You'll own credit and CLtV modelling projects end to end, from spotting where the modelling stack is holding the business back through to landing the change. The work spans keeping production models healthy, incremental development, and research that reshapes how the models work. AI has lowered the cost of prototyping enough that ideas which used to sit below the priority line are now viable, so the R&D share of the role is growing.

Live examples of the work:

  • Causal estimation of offer terms. Modelling how amount, duration, and price shape customer outcomes.

  • Unifying auto and manual models. The two families were built without forced technical alignment. Finding a principled way to unify them on a common cost function is open work.

  • IFRS accounting model. A multi-stage credit model where information propagates back from later-stage recovery predictions to sharpen upfront loss estimates.

  • Generalising credit and CLtV. Whether a more general framing could replace both separate models is an open research question.

The requirements

Essential:

  • Communication. You write and speak clearly, directly, and concisely. You adapt technical detail to your audience.

  • Statistical foundations. You have a background in probability and statistics from a quantitative field. You reason about uncertainty and calibration as first-order concerns.

  • Production ML. You have built and shipped supervised ML models end to end – exploration, training, deployment, monitoring.

  • Research mindset. You proactively explore new ways to add value. R&D time is when you expect to find the next step change.

  • Judgement. You critically evaluate model output – yours, a colleague's, or an LLM's – and can explain why a choice is right. You defend your reasoning under challenge, and challenge others' when the evidence points elsewhere. You've influenced technical direction beyond your own projects.

  • Project leadership. You've owned modelling projects end to end, from spotting the opportunity through framing, method choice, shipping, and landing the commercial impact. You move fast, iterate, and update on new evidence rather than chase perfection.

  • AI fluency. You use AI as a primary tool. You prototype with it, automate with it, and take on R&D that would not otherwise be viable. You use judgement on where it helps and where it doesn't.

Bonus:

  • Domain experience. You have worked in credit risk, lending, or customer lifetime value modelling.

  • Non-linear methods. You have shipped gradient boosting or neural networks on tabular data in production.

  • Bayesian methods. You have used hierarchical models, MCMC, or Bayesian updating in real work.

  • Time series modelling. You have modelled temporal data where autocorrelation, drift, or seasonality mattered.

  • Python. The stack the team uses.

The salary

We expect to pay from £90,000 – £120,000 for this role. But, we’re open-minded, so definitely include your salary goals with your application. We routinely benchmark salaries against market rates, and run quarterly performance and salary reviews.

The culture

At iwoca, the best idea wins. We model our culture on independent thinking, challenging untested logic, and evidence-based decisions. We prioritise learning and growth, and give people the autonomy to develop in the direction that makes them most effective.

We're a tech company and believe in the power of AI to help us work faster and better. We provide the infrastructure where every iwocan always has access to the best models and where those models have access to all of our data. We will help our people to learn how to use and grow with the new tools available to them.

The offices

  • Events and community-led groups, including running groups, padel, and monthly ping-pong and pool competitions.

raw.description:
About Juicebox

Juicebox is on a mission to help teams win the talent war.

In the age of AI, human ingenuity is the ultimate scarce resource. Recruiting is a zero-sum game where you either compete or lose.

Teams at Ramp, Notion, and leading AI labs use Juicebox to power their hiring, alongside 5,000+ customers from early-stage startups to Fortune 500 companies.

We are on the path to $100M in ARR with 20%+ monthly growth, powering thousands of searches every day and making Juicebox one of the fastest-growing AI SaaS companies in the world.

Juicebox has raised over $116M in funding from lead investors including Sequoia Capital, DST Global, and NFDG. Read more about our $80M Series B here. Additional investors in Juicebox include Y Combinator, Coatue, Bond, Lux, Verified Capital, and Committed Capital.

About the Role

As an Account Executive at Juicebox, you'll play a foundational role in launching our London office and building our go-to-market presence across Europe. As one of our first Account Executives in the region, you'll have the opportunity to shape our sales motion, influence how we serve European customers, and help establish Juicebox as a leader in AI-powered recruiting.

Our go-to-market motion is highly product-led. We generate 200+ inbound demo requests every month through our free trial and demo experience, giving you the opportunity to focus on building relationships and closing business rather than generating outbound pipeline. You'll sell primarily to Talent Acquisition, People, and Recruiting leaders, while also expanding relationships across our growing base of 2,000+ customers. We move quickly, with typical sales cycles of just 2 to 3 weeks, and consistently win against legacy recruiting solutions.

You Will…

  • Own the full sales cycle from discovery through negotiation and close across the European market.

  • Help establish and scale Juicebox's go-to-market presence as part of our founding London team.

  • Convert inbound demo requests and free trial users into long-term customers.

  • Partner with Talent Acquisition, People, and Recruiting leaders to understand their hiring challenges and recommend solutions.

  • Identify expansion opportunities within our growing customer base.

  • Collaborate closely with marketing, customer success, and product to refine our European go-to-market strategy.

  • Maintain accurate pipeline forecasts and CRM hygiene.

  • Share customer insights to help shape our product roadmap and regional growth strategy.

You Have…

  • 2+ years of experience closing SaaS deals.

  • Experience selling deals with annual contract values (ACVs) between £10,000 and £50,000.

  • A track record of consistently exceeding quota (President's Club, Top Performer, Top 10%, MVP, or similar achievements).

  • Strong discovery, negotiation, and relationship-building skills.

  • Excellent communication skills and a customer-first mindset.

  • A bias toward action and the ability to thrive in a fast-paced startup environment.

  • Located in or willing to relocate to London.

Bonus Points If You…

  • You've sold to Talent Acquisition, People, HR, or Recruiting leaders.

  • You have experience in a product-led growth (PLG) sales environment.

  • You've worked on a small, high-performing GTM team where ownership and collaboration were critical.

  • You have experience selling AI, recruiting, or HR technology solutions.

Perks & Benefits for all Full Time Employees

  • Top-of-market compensation with meaningful equity, because everyone should share in our success.

  • Daily meals provided: breakfast catering, lunch order via DoorDash corporate, and for those who like to work late, dinner if staying after 7pm

For US Employees:

  • Comprehensive healthcare with 100% employer-paid medical coverage for employees (PPO Platinum plan with $0 deductible). 90% employer contribution for dependents. Dental & Vision: 90% employer covered; 85% for dependents.

  • $2,000 annual wellness stipend to support your physical, mental, and financial well-being.

  • $300/month commuting stipend to help cover the cost of getting to and from the office.

For UK Employees:

  • Comprehensive private medical insurance with £0 excess, full outpatient cover, comprehensive cancer care, mental health treatment, and 24/7 GP access.

  • £1,500 annual wellness stipend to support your physical, mental, and financial well-being

  • £3,500/year commuting stipend to help cover the cost of getting to and from the office.

THE COMPANY:

Juul Labs's mission is to transition the world's billion adult smokers away from combustible cigarettes, eliminate their use, and combat underage usage of our products. We have the opportunity to address one of the world's most intractable challenges through a commitment to exceptional quality, research, design, and innovation. Backed by leading technology investors, we are committed to the same excellence when it comes to hiring great talent.

We are a diverse team that is united by this common purpose and we are hiring the world's best engineers, scientists, designers, product managers, operations experts, and customer service and business professionals. If the opportunity to build your career is compelling, read on for more details.

ROLE AND RESPONSIBILITIES:

Reporting to the Head of Field Sales, the Senior City Development Manager is the lead field operator for key strategic cities. Bringing strong commercial experience, this hands-on role combines city strategy, regional key account management, and specialist product knowledge to ensure field activity is tailored, scaled, and executed effectively. As well as taking primary ownership of their own city performance - driving awareness, distribution, trade execution, and market share - the role provides commercial coaching and practical support to City Development Managers across the region.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

Commercial Delivery & Strategic Customer Management

  • Account Management: Take ownership of regional key account operators and on-the-ground route-to-market partnerships. Build strong commercial relationships that drive long-term growth across distribution, execution, education, and rate-of-sale.
  • Commercial Coaching: Act as a commercial sounding board for City Development Managers. Offer practical advice, coaching, and support on account planning, negotiating, and working through local trade challenges.
  • Commercial Tools: Create, refine, and deploy practical commercial sales tools (e.g., commercial calculators, regional activity, customer and channel propositions) that address ground-level field challenges and help field teams and CDMs win across regions.
  • Regional Development: Build relationships and develop non-traditional trade channels, tailoring the approach to fit local market nuances while ensuring all partnerships align with company goals and regulatory requirements.
  • Execution Standards: Set the operational benchmark for distribution, brand visibility, and advocacy across all trade channels (including priority regional accounts, Wholesale, Vape, and alternative channels). Measure and evaluate execution quality across key cities, establishing clear guidelines and sharing proven approaches to help CDMs elevate standards across their own territories.

City Strategy & Execution

  • City Strategy: Adapt national frameworks into practical, city-specific plans that reflect local demographics, trade setups, and regional key account footprints. Identify what each specific city needs to win, ensuring resources are deployed effectively.
  • CDM Guidance: support CDMs in analysing their own cities, adapting national plans to fit their city's specific dynamics, and executing tailored activity efficiently. 
  • Third-Party Prioritisation: Work alongside and co-ordinate third-party field teams on a city-by-city basis, making sure field resources are directed to where the local opportunity is greatest.
  • Events & Activations: Identify and execute local promotional activity and trade programmes, designed specifically around the local target audience to drive engagement, product education, and sales.
  • Performance Ownership: drive city performance and manage risks and opportunities in your region
  • Field Insight & Strategy: Link field execution with the Head of Field Sales by translating plans into action, while feeding back trade realities, competitor moves, and new channel opportunities to shape national strategy.

YOUR PROFILE: Personal and Professional Qualifications

  • 3-5 years' experience in a similar role or commercial setting
  • Commercial Acumen & Account Management: Strong track record in account management alongside experience handling multi-site accounts that span across adjacent territories. Proven ability to negotiate, drive sales volume, distribution, and market share. Ability to adapt style to both existing and new channels and opportunities. 
  • Commercial Coaching & Regional Influence: Proven ability to influence and mentor peers by sharing commercial expertise, guiding regional key account negotiations, and helping tailor city plans, all while supporting established line-management structures.
  • Commercial Tools: Experience developing practical sales tools and toolkits to solve local trade challenges and drive regional growth.
  • Execution & Quality Evaluation: Skilled at turning ideas into reality by tailoring local activations, brand, and direct engagement opportunities to fit specific city needs. Proven ability to measure and evaluate sales return, and provide analysis to inform future execution standards
  • Commercial Analysis & Problem Solving: Skilled at analysing city sales data and trade trends to spot commercial gaps, fix underperforming territories, and feed clear market feedback to the Head of Field Sales.
  • Self-Driven & Resilient: Challenges the status quo, takes decisive action, and turns ideas into commercial results in changing environments. 
  • A full UK driving licence is required for this role. 
  • Education: BA/BS degree preferred but not required

JUUL LABS PERKS & BENEFITS: 

  • A place to grow your career. We'll help you set big goals - and exceed them
  • People. Work with talented, committed and supportive teammates
  • Equity and performance bonuses. Every employee is a stakeholder in our success
  • Location. Field based with a requirement to be in the London office when required
Juul Labs is proud to be an equal opportunity employer and is committed to creating a diverse and inclusive work environment for all employees and job applicants, without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, age, gender identity or gender expression, national origin, disability or veteran status. We will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records, pursuant to the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance. raw.description:
About Kernel

Agents are starting to sell, buy and operate on behalf of companies. But before an agent can close a deal, qualify an account, route a lead or assess risk, it has to answer a basic question: which company is this?

Today, that answer is messy, and no one answers it reliably. Business identity lives across CRMs, ERPs and third-party datasets full of duplicates, missing parent companies, stale addresses and incorrect enrichment. The cost shows up across the enterprise: sales teams miss revenue opportunities because they lack the right account context; operations teams take on avoidable exposure because risk signals are fragmented or wrong; and finance teams end up chasing, writing off, or defaulting on bad debt that should have been caught earlier.

Humans have worked around that mess for years. Agents cannot. They need a reliable business identity layer they can trust.

Kernel is building that layer: the business registry for agents. We issue a permanent Kernel ID for every business, plus the context an agent needs to act on it. Ops, data and revenue teams at Gong, Legora, Mistral, Canva and Notion already use Kernel on their own systems. Agents are next, and there will be far more of them.

We have raised $20M from top VCs and operators at Plaid, OpenAI, Slack and others, and we are growing 10x YoY.

The Role

We’re looking for an AI Ops Engineer to build the internal systems that help Kernel scale without adding unnecessary manual work. You’ll work across GTM, Marketing, Customer Success and Operations - finding the highest-leverage problems and building practical AI-powered workflows.

This is a hands-on builder role. You’ll take ideas from a vague business problem to a tool or workflow that people use, then maintain and improve it in production. You’ll choose the fastest sensible approach for each problem - coding agents, automation platforms, APIs, data pipelines or lightweight code.

You’ll report to Arvin Ashrafi, Head of Finance & Operations, and partner closely with GTM, Marketing, and Customer Success leadership.

What You’ll Be Doing

  • Define how an AI-native company operates: help build Kernel’s internal playbook for using AI across GTM, Marketing, Customer Success and Operations

raw.title: Senior Product Manager - Containers & Automotive Intelligence
raw.description:
At Kpler, we are dedicated to helping our clients navigate complex markets with ease. By simplifying global trade information and providing valuable insights, we empower organisations to make informed decisions in commodities, energy, and maritime sectors.
 
Since our founding in 2014, we have focused on delivering top-tier intelligence through user-friendly platforms. Our team of over 850 experts from 69 countries works tirelessly to transform intricate data into actionable strategies, ensuring our clients stay ahead in a dynamic market landscape. Join us to leverage cutting-edge innovation for impactful results and experience unparalleled support on your journey to success.
 

Kpler is expanding its Maritime & Logistics offering through two complementary products: Container Intelligence and Automotive Intelligence. Container Intelligence builds on Kpler’s existing container tracking capabilities, providing per-container ocean visibility alongside insights into terminal congestion, queues, stay and wait times, and predictive vessel ETAs and ETDs. Automotive Intelligence represents a new product opportunity, transforming Kpler’s data into a dedicated workspace for the automotive sector.

As a Senior Product Manager, Container & Automotive Intelligence, you will own both products end to end, balancing the growth of an established offering with the development and launch of a new product from the ground up. Working closely with the Lead Product Manager – Maritime & Logistics, Engineering, Data, Sales, Marketing and sector teams, you will define product strategy, prioritise roadmaps, lead customer discovery and drive go-to-market execution.

For Container Intelligence, your focus will be on expanding product capabilities, improving prediction quality and coverage, and increasing customer adoption and commercial growth. For Automotive Intelligence, you will work with the Automotive Sector Lead, Data Engineers and Automotive Analyst to shape the product strategy, define the initial offering and deliver a first release targeted for early 2027.

This is an individual-contributor role for an experienced product professional who can manage multiple workstreams in parallel, make clear trade-offs and deliver data-driven products in an evolving market. You will be expected to take a pragmatic, iterative approach, launching products and capabilities efficiently before continuously improving them through customer feedback and market insights.


Key Responsibilities
  • Own the product strategy and roadmap for Container Intelligence and Automotive Intelligence, balancing customer needs, commercial impact, development effort and data readiness across both products.
  • Drive delivery across both product teams, maintaining clear priorities, healthy backlogs and predictable release cadences while making trade-offs explicit when competing priorities arise.
  • Lead customer discovery across both segments, translating customer feedback and market opportunities into prioritised product requirements and roadmap decisions.
  • Collaborate with Engineering, Data, Sales, Customer Success, Product Marketing and sector teams to align product development, share capabilities and deliver customer value.
  • Optimise Container Intelligence by expanding terminal congestion, dwell-time and vessel ETA/ETD prediction capabilities, improving data coverage and prediction quality across the web application and API.
  • Build Automotive Intelligence from the ground up, translating sector strategy and customer needs into a product roadmap, epics, user stories and acceptance criteria across seven intelligence modules.
  • Define the Automotive Intelligence workspace, bringing together trade flows and lane capacity, schedule reliability, fleet supply and renewal, charter rates and asset values, ports and terminals, and fuel, emissions, CII and bunkering insights into an actionable product experience.
  • Drive go-to-market execution for both products, working with Product Marketing on positioning, packaging, pricing input and launch planning, while securing design partners and supporting early customer adoption for Automotive Intelligence.
  • Establish clear product success metrics and trusted methodologies, tracking adoption, engagement, customer outcomes, ARR and customer logos, and using performance insights to guide ongoing product development.

    • Skills & Experience
  • 6–10 years of senior product management experience in a B2B data, analytics or SaaS environment, with a proven track record of delivering products that customers adopt.
  • Experience managing multiple products or workstreams simultaneously, including taking a product from concept to launch while growing an existing product in the market.
  • Experience working with data-heavy products, with an understanding of data sources, pipelines, technical dependencies and their implications for product strategy and delivery.
  • Strong product discovery skills, with the ability to translate customer needs and market insights into clear product direction and prioritised roadmaps.
  • Experience working closely with Engineering and Data teams to deliver data-driven products.
  • Relevant experience in maritime, shipping, container logistics, automotive or trade intelligence, with an understanding of concepts such as AIS, ports and terminals, ETA prediction and emissions regulation, including EU ETS, FuelEU Maritime and CII.
  • Experience with product roadmap prioritisation, backlog ownership and delivery planning across multiple teams or workstreams.
  • Understanding of go-to-market planning, including product positioning, packaging and pricing input.
  • Strong stakeholder management and communication skills, with the ability to engage technical and commercial teams and external customers.
  • A self-directed and decisive approach, with the ability to make trade-offs, take ownership of outcomes and operate with limited supervision.
  • A pragmatic, action-oriented mindset, with the ability to work in ambiguous environments and deliver iteratively.

    • Nice to have
  • Experience developing and managing API-based products.
  • An established network across shippers, freight forwarders, carriers, car manufacturers or car carriers.
  • Familiarity with container movements, voyage legs, port calls and wider maritime and trade data concepts.
  • Experience using product management tools such as Jira and Confluence.
