raw.description:
We are seeking an Chief Platform Architect in our CO, MN, or UK locations.
 
As the Chief Platform Architect for the Quantum Software Developer Platform, you will act as the technical authority for the design Quantinuum’s developer platform: access portals for quantum computers, hybrid work-flow orchestration, tooling access, documentation, and security. You will work with other leaders on hardware-software co-design efforts, ensuring our platform is scalable and enabling of our quantum processors. You will mentor senior engineers, ensure excellent coding standards, and help define and execute on the technical roadmap to translate business needs into robust, production-ready systems.

Key Responsibilities:
  • Own the design and specifications of a high-performance developer platform.
  • Refine quantum computer access API and web portal architecture for performance, scalability and multi-region operation
  • Transform web portal into an application development and delivery framework by leveraging cloud-based hybrid workflow engine and reusable quantum/classical application components
  • Define standard interfaces for hosting application components and building applications by both internal and external developers
  • Ensure the security and reliability of the platform as it scales up
  • Deliver customizable cloud-based hybrid applications to end users
  • Work across the business to help define and maintain the technology roadmap, translating business goals into technical requirements and evaluating new technologies.
  • Foster a culture of excellence by establishing best coding practices, performing architectural reviews, and mentoring senior software engineers.

    • YOU MUST HAVE:
  • 25+ years in software engineering, with at least 5+ years in a senior architect or lead role, specifically within developer platforms.

    • WE VALUE:
  • Deep knowledge of cloud platforms (AWS, Azure, or GCP) and cloud-native solutions.
  • Expertise in CI/CD pipeline design, developer portals (e.g., Backstage), and observability tools.
  • Demonstrated success in designing large-scale software systems
  • Proven ability to lead architectural work for large-scale projects and influence teams without direct authority.
  • Excellent communication skills, with the ability to explain complex technical concepts to both technical and non-technical stakeholders.
  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field; Master’s or PhD preferred.
    Preferred Qualifications
  • Prior experience in the design and architecture of developer platforms
  • Experience in building platform engineering teams from the ground up.
  • Background in Site Reliability Engineering (SRE).
  • Record of publication or patents in quantum computing.

    • Quantinuum is a leading quantum computing company delivering a full stack platform designed to make quantum computing deployable in real-world environments. With active engagements spanning pharmaceuticals, material science, financial services, government, industrial sectors, and leading academic and research institutions worldwide, we are helping organizations unlock the transformative potential of quantum computing. 

    Our global team of more than 800 employees includes many of the world's leading scientists, engineers, and researchers, with more than 70% of our technology team holding advanced degrees at the Master's or PhD level. Headquartered in Broomfield, Colorado, Quantinuum operates across the United States, United Kingdom, Germany, Japan, and Singapore. 

    By joining Quantinuum, you’ll help shape the future of quantum computing, pushing the limits of technology, and making the impossible possible.

    What’s in it for you?

    We believe our people are our greatest strength and offer a comprehensive rewards package that supports your professional growth, well-being, and long-term success.

    • Competitive compensation and the opportunity to work on groundbreaking technology
    • Flexible work arrangements that support work-life balance
    • Employer-subsidized medical, dental, and vision insurance
    • 401(k) retirement savings plan with company match and student loan repayment benefit
    • Equity opportunities
    • Generous paid time off, sick leave, and 12 paid holidays annually
    • Paid parental leave
    • Employee discount programs 

    Equal Opportunity Employer

    Quantinuum is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to building an inclusive workplace where all employees and applicants are treated with respect and provided equal opportunities regardless of race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, ancestry, marital status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

raw.description:
Who are we?

Smarkets: Predicting the Future of Betting

Smarkets is a prediction market exchange for sports and political trading, having handled over $50 billion in volume since 2010. We're upending sports betting with the fairest prices, the best technology, and a superior customer experience, powered by attracting great people and building a high-performance environment where they thrive. We're looking for an atypical candidate with strong regulated-business experience to support our growing CFTC business.

The Team

Security sits within Infrastructure and Engineering, protecting the distributed, real-time systems behind our trading engine. The team's remit spans our core products and our DCM/DCO entities, with a real regulatory dimension to the work, particularly around our CFTC-regulated business units. Alongside that regulatory scope, the focus is squarely on hands-on engineering: designing, building, and shipping the security tooling and controls that let engineering teams move fast safely.

About the Role:

This is a founding build. You'll stand up security engineering from the ground up through go-live and mature it as we scale, working within Infrastructure and Engineering teams to build the controls, automation, and guardrails our trading systems and regulated entities need.

What you will do:

  • Build the Foundations: Be part of a founding build, standing up security engineering from the ground up through go-live and maturing it as we scale, working within Infrastructure and Engineering teams.

  • Design Guardrails: Design, build, and deploy security controls and guardrails across cloud-native platforms, including AI security solutions protecting customer-facing and internal products.

If you're ready to help shape the future of prediction markets with cutting-edge technology and a customer-first philosophy, Smarkets is where you belong.

raw.title: Associate Implementation Consultant
raw.description:
Unleash AI Innovators, Securely

Software is being rewritten in real time. AI agents are starting to write more code than humans do, at a speed no security team has ever had to match, and that single shift is opening up the biggest opportunity our industry has seen in a decade. We're not bracing for it, we're building the company that owns it.

Snyk is building the next generation security platform where security isn't a set of tools people operate. It's a team of security agents working alongside your engineers, finding, fixing, and governing risk at the speed software is now built. These agents work alongside both the company build and the agents they adopt. Security stops being a queue of work waiting for people, and becomes a coordinated workforce companies direct and trust.

Job Summary

Snyk is hiring an Associate Implementation Consultant to help enterprise customers get started with the Snyk platform after the sale. You will support and deliver onboarding engagements, working with customer development and security teams to configure Snyk across their SDLC, CI/CD pipelines, and cloud infrastructure. This is an early-career role for someone with a technical foundation who wants to build a career in customer-facing application security, with hands-on work from your first weeks and structured coaching from experienced consultants along the way.

About the Team

The Customer Solutions team owns the technical success of Snyk's customers after the deal closes, from first onboarding session through full platform adoption. Implementation Consultants work alongside Technical Success, Support, Sales, and Product to turn a customer's security goals into a deployed, measurable program. As Snyk's install base continues to grow, this team is expanding to keep delivering a world-class onboarding experience at scale.

What You’ll Do

  • Deliver onboarding engagements for customers with well-defined requirements, following Snyk's onboarding methodology from kick-off through closure.

  • Support senior consultants on larger and more complex implementations, taking ownership of defined workstreams and learning how enterprise rollouts are planned and run.

  • Configure and integrate the Snyk platform with customer source control, CI/CD, container, and cloud environments, working from documented procedures and escalating questions early.

  • Join customer kick-offs, working sessions, and status reviews, and keep customer contacts informed on progress and next steps.

  • Answer customer questions about how Snyk works, and bring in senior consultants, Support, or Product when an issue needs deeper expertise.

  • Keep accurate project plans, notes, and handoff documentation so every engagement is easy for others to pick up.

  • Use Snyk's onboarding playbooks and templates, and suggest improvements when you find gaps.

  • Troubleshoot common integration and configuration issues, and document what you learn for the rest of the team.

  • Help customer teams understand developer-first security practices so they keep using Snyk after onboarding ends.

  • Build your skills through regular coaching, shadowing, and Snyk's technical training and certification programs.

What you’ll bring

  • 1+ years in technical consulting, professional services, technical support, or another customer-facing technical role, or equivalent hands-on experience such as an internship or relevant projects.

  • Foundational knowledge of the SDLC and modern DevOps practices, and curiosity about where security fits into both.

  • Familiarity with CI/CD and DevOps tooling (for example Jenkins, GitHub Actions, GitLab, Azure DevOps, Kubernetes), with the motivation to go deeper.

  • Ability to manage your own tasks and deadlines across more than one customer project, with support from your team.

  • The ability to explain technical topics clearly to developers and other technical contacts, in writing and in conversation.

  • Genuine interest in application security and belief that a developer-first approach is the right way to solve it.

  • A collaborative, customer-first approach and a willingness to ask questions, take feedback, and learn quickly.

  • Working fluency with AI-assisted tools (Claude, Gemini, or similar) and comfort with how AI-generated code is changing what customers need to secure.

  • Strong written and verbal communication, plus an organized approach to problem solving.

  • Nice to have: basic proficiency in a scripting language such as Python, JavaScript, or another modern language.

  • Nice to have: prior experience in a support, solutions engineering, or technical account role for AppSec, CI, or DevSecOps products.

  • Nice to have: a security certification such as Security+, CSSLP, or CEH.

  • Nice to have: a Project Management Professional (PMP) or CAPM certification, or equivalent project management coursework.

  • Nice to have: a Computer Science degree or equivalent programming background, and exposure to enterprise-scale web technologies and microservices.

About Snyk

Snyk is committed to creating an inclusive and engaging environment where our employees can thrive as we rally behind our common mission to make the digital world a safer place. From Snyk employee resource groups, to global benefits that help our employees prioritize their health, wellness, financial security, and a work/life blend, we aim to support our employees along their entire journeys here at Snyk.

Equal Employment Opportunity

Snyk is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, or status as a protected veteran.

raw.description:

Sonar is driving the future of agent-centric software development. As the leader in AI code verification and governance, we solve a critical problem: ensuring that software generated by AI-assisted developers or autonomous agents is reliable, secure, and maintainable.

Integrating seamlessly with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, Gemini, and Devin, we help over 75% of the Fortune 100 build trusted, reliable, compliant software. Customers who use Sonar are 44% less likely to report an outage due to AI-generated code.

We believe code verification is the critical missing link in the Agent-Centric Development Cycle (AC/DC). Industry giants like Nvidia, ServiceNow, Booking.com, Goldman Sachs, AstraZeneca, and Ford Motor Company count on us to provide independent, explainable, consistent review and governance of their AI-generated code via products like:

  • SonarQube: The world’s leading AI code review and verification platform.
  • SonarQube Foundation Agent: Currently topping the leaderboards for agentic software repair.
  • SonarSweep & Sonar Context Augmentation: Providing the enterprise-grade context and constraints agents need to be truly effective.

Our team operates across global hubs in Austin, Bochum, Dubai, Geneva, London, Singapore, Tokyo, and Washington D.C. We move with a mindset we call CODE:

  • Committed to our customers and community.
  • Obsessed with quality.
  • Deliberate in our decisions.
  • Effective as one team.

With over $400M in revenue and profitable, fast-paced growth, we are building the backbone of the AI software revolution. If you’re hungry to have an impact, want to build at a fast pace, and ready to work at the forefront of AI, we want to hear from you.


Position description

As Director of Revenue Enablement, you will lead the global enablement function across Sonar's go-to-market organisation, spanning Sales, Customer Success, and Partner teams. Reporting to the VP of Revenue Operations, you will own the strategy, programmes, and systems that shorten ramp time, lift quota attainment, and equip our GTM teams to sell a technical product into developer, platform, and security buyers. You will inherit a small enablement team and a strong foundation, and will scale it into a measurable, outcomes-driven function that supports Sonar's next phase of growth in the age of agent-centric development.


What you will do

  • Own the revenue enablement strategy: Define and execute a multi-year enablement roadmap aligned to Sonar's GTM priorities, with quarterly outcomes tied to ramp time, win rate, and quota attainment.

  • Lead a global enablement team: Manage and grow a team of enablement specialists across regions; set clear priorities, coach for excellence, and operate as a player-coach where required.

  • Design onboarding and ongoing readiness: Build role-based onboarding for Sales, CS, and Partner roles. Run continuous readiness programmes across product, process, messaging, and selling skills.

  • Equip teams for a technical buyer: Build playbooks, talk tracks, objection-handling guides, and competitive content tailored to developer, platform engineering, DevSecOps, and CISO audiences.

  • Drive GTM kick-off and major moments: Own the enablement track for Sonar's annual GTM kick-off (250+ attendees) and quarterly business reviews.

  • Modernise the enablement tech stack: Evaluate and operate the LMS, CMS, sales engagement, conversation intelligence, and AI tooling that power seller workflows. Drive adoption and measure impact.

  • Partner cross-functionally: Work with the CRO, VP Sales, VP CS, Product Marketing, Product, and Partner leaders to align messaging, qualification frameworks, and customer journey execution.

  • Measure what matters: Build dashboards and reporting that link enablement activity to GTM outcomes. Use data to prioritise investment and retire programmes that do not move the number.

  • Embed AI into the seller workflow: Bring a clear point of view on how AI tooling accelerates rep productivity, coaching, and deal execution at Sonar.


Experience and Qualifications

The ideal candidate will:

  • Bring 10+ years in B2B SaaS revenue or sales enablement, including 4+ years leading a global enablement function.

  • Have a demonstrated track record of improving ramp time, win rate, and quota attainment through structured, measurable programmes.

  • Have enabled GTM teams selling a technical product to developer, platform engineering, DevOps, DevSecOps, or security buyers.

  • Have designed and run large-scale GTM kick-offs and enablement events for 250+ attendees.

  • Be hands-on with the modern enablement tech stack (LMS, CMS, sales engagement, conversation intelligence) and have integrated AI tooling into seller workflows.

  • Be fluent with at least one structured qualification framework (MEDDPICC, Command of the Message, or equivalent) and able to drive consistent adoption across the field.

  • Operate effectively with VP and C-level stakeholders, and bring strong written and facilitation skills.

  • Balance strategic thinking with hands-on execution in a fast-paced, high-growth environment.

  • Be passionate about building inclusive, high-performing teams.

In-office Culture

 

We're intentional about this. We believe the best teams are built in the room together. Three anchor days — Mondays, Tuesdays, and Thursdays — create the collaboration rhythm that makes a hub office worth having.

Candidates need to be genuinely based in the location the role is posted — if that's not where you are today, we're happy to support relocation for the right person.

And because we're growing fast, you'll accelerate your career with a level of ownership and impact you simply won't get at bigger, slower-moving companies.

Account Director

Sparta Commodities is the next generation, AI-first commodity trading data platform. We are revolutionising energy commodity trading, delivering market intelligence that empowers traders and analysts across all energy verticals.

We’re looking for an Account Director to own some of Sparta’s largest and most important client relationships. You’ll have two jobs. First, protect the revenue: keep every account deeply engaged, from the traders and analysts using Sparta every day up to the most senior decision-makers, so that no renewal ever comes as a surprise. Second, and just as important, grow these accounts into $1M+ relationships. This is a true sales role. You’ll find the opportunities yourself, build the business case and lead senior-level conversations that move clients from limited user licences to enterprise-wide, unlimited-user agreements.

What You’ll Be Doing

Protect and deepen the relationship

  • Own a portfolio of Sparta’s largest and most strategic accounts as the senior commercial lead for each one.

  • Build relationships across the whole organisation, from day-to-day users on the trading desk to heads of trading, COOs and C-suite stakeholders.

  • Know every account well enough that renewals are never at risk by surprise. Track usage, engagement and stakeholder sentiment, and act early on any sign of risk.

  • Run executive business reviews that show the value Sparta delivers and agree with each client what success looks like next.

  • Work with Customer Success, Product and our analyst teams so every client gets full value from Sparta and their feedback shapes the product roadmap.

Grow accounts into $1M+ relationships

  • Build and execute a strategic account plan for every account, mapping desks, teams, regions and commodity verticals not yet using Sparta.
    Identify and close upsell and cross-sell opportunities proactively, including additional products, verticals, desks and users.

  • Take conversations to the most senior level and lead strategic discussions about moving accounts from limited user licences to enterprise-level, unlimited-user agreements.

  • Use value selling to build the business case for enterprise adoption, showing how Sparta changes the way the whole organisation trades, analyses and makes decisions.

  • Run complex, multi-stakeholder deals from start to finish, including procurement, legal and commercial negotiation.

  • Consistently meet or beat retention, net revenue retention and expansion targets.

  • Keep account plans, renewals and expansion pipeline accurate and up to date in HubSpot, including MEDDPICC qualification and forecasting.

  • Coach and support Account Managers, sharing best practice on strategic account management.

About You

  • 8+ years’ experience growing existing and strategic accounts in B2B SaaS, financial data, market intelligence or commodities.

  • A proven record of expanding large accounts substantially, including taking accounts into seven-figure or enterprise-wide agreements.

  • The gravitas and credibility to lead conversations with very senior stakeholders, including heads of trading, COOs and C-suite executives, and to challenge their thinking with confidence.

  • Strong skills in value selling. You build the business case around the client’s outcomes, not product features, and can show how Sparta changes their operations at enterprise level.

  • Experience leading complex, multi-stakeholder enterprise negotiations through procurement and legal.

  • Hands-on ownership of both retention and expansion. You run the renewal and close the growth yourself.

  • Strategic and commercially sharp, with the discipline to build and run long-term account plans.

  • Organised and data-driven, with strong CRM and forecasting habits and a working knowledge of AI tools.

  • Genuinely curious about commodities and energy markets.

Nice to Have Experience

  • Prior experience selling to trading houses, oil majors, refiners, banks or hedge funds.

  • Experience with MEDDPICC, Command of the Message or another value-selling framework.

  • Familiarity with HubSpot and Claude.

  • An additional European language.

Why Join Sparta?

At Sparta, our culture is built on innovation, collaboration, and high performance. We thrive in a fast-paced environment where initiative is celebrated, challenges are embraced, and impact is rewarded.

• Equity in a high-growth, VC-backed company

• $42M in Series B funding — strong market traction and investment

• Early-stage growth — build your career as we scale

• Market-leading product — we are redefining commodity trading intelligence

• Top-tier tools and technology to support your success

What's the Culture Like at Sparta?

At Sparta, our culture isn't just a set of values on a wall — it's how we work. We embrace a dynamic environment where initiative is celebrated, challenges are met head-on, and innovation thrives. You'll collaborate with people who are passionate about our mission and committed to building outstanding products and outcomes for our customers.

The Sparta Code

Understanding is non-negotiable

Understanding leads to believing. Believing leads to winning.

The 'why' is the difference between compliance and conviction. Before we execute, we ask: why does this matter, who does it serve, what changes if we win? People who understand the mission don't need to be managed.

Ask for forgiveness, not for permission

Most decisions are reversible. Most fears are not.

90% of decisions are reversible. Make them, ship, iterate. Perfection is the enemy of efficiency. Bias for action means moving before you have all the answers, but it isn't recklessness. The rule: tell the rest of us what you did, what changed, what you learned.

Fall in love with the problem

The mission wins. Your idea doesn't have to.

Solutions flatter our ego. They feel like progress. But solutions without problems are opinions, and opinions don't move customers, markets, or teammates. The goal is to find what's true, not to win the room. If your idea gets killed because a better one comes along, that's the system working.

It's your fault. Lucky you.

If it's on you, it's in your control.

True ownership sounds harsh until you feel how liberating it is. If every problem is yours, you stop spending energy on who to blame and start spending it on how to fix it. Effective leaders default to 'it's on me'. Not out of guilt, but out of agency.

Conflict is a gift

Honesty is an expression of care.

Withholding feedback is choosing comfort over growth, yours and your colleague's. Staying silent deprives others of the chance to learn. We challenge openly and with positive intent. Done with care, this builds trust. Done with ego, it destroys it.

Sparta is the AI leader for commodity trading, home to Leonidas AI, the first operating system for oil and commodity traders.

Backed by $42 million in Series B funding led by One Peak, with participation from returning investors FirstMark and Singular, the same investors behind AI leaders like Legora, Dataiku, and Synthesia. Most companies are building a chatbot on top of data. We've built an agent with an actual reasoning layer, grounded in years of proprietary market data and in-house trading expertise nobody else has.

We're scaling fast, and it's an exciting time to join. From independents to multinationals, the world's leading commodity teams use Sparta and Leonidas AI to move faster, trade smarter, and stay ahead of the market.

At Sparta, you'll be trusted to take ownership, backed by a team who wants you to succeed. AI is how we build here, not just what we sell. Good ideas move fast, and yours could go from staging to production in a couple of hours, whatever department you're in. You'll be challenged, supported, and given room to grow, building the AI that's changing how commodity trading gets done.

Your work has reach. From shaping Leonidas AI, to powering smarter decisions for traders around the world, to changing how commodity trading is done. And because we're growing fast, you'll accelerate your career with a level of ownership and impact you simply won't get at bigger, slower-moving companies.


At Sparta, we’re on a mission to build the next generation of commodity trading platforms - replacing the fragmented tools that traders typically rely on with a single, powerful dashboard. Our product is a data-driven platform that aggregates real-time feeds from across the commodities domain, transforming them into intuitive, actionable visualisations within one unified interface. Users can explore pre-built data views or define their own custom formulas to create tailored insights.

To deliver on this vision, our engineers tackle real distributed systems problems on a daily basis, where designing for reliability and performance at scale is essential to a seamless user experience. As we unlock the next level of scale, those problems get harder and more interesting. This role is for an engineer who wants to own meaningful parts of that system now, and grow into the technical decisions that shape it.

We’re looking for people who thrive in an empowered environment - engineers who are comfortable being given problems to solve rather than solutions to implement. You should enjoy working at pace, value autonomy, and prefer to ask for forgiveness rather than permission. You won’t be handed tickets. You’ll be handed context, and trusted to work out the right thing to build.

Whereas Sparta is a remote-first company, for this role we’re looking for someone who values a hybrid working style, which in a typical week could involve spending a couple of days in the office - with flexibility built in.


WHAT YOU’LL BE DOING:

  • Design, build and maintain the backend services behind our real-time and analytical data processing.

  • Own features end to end, from shaping the approach to running them in production.

  • Optimise pipelines and services for low latency, high throughput and scale.

  • Work with engineers, product and stakeholders to stay aligned on direction.

  • Contribute to design reviews with a clear view on the trade-offs.

  • Keep your services healthy - observability, feedback loops, incident response.

  • Raise the bar around you through code review, pairing and knowledge sharing.


ABOUT YOU:

  • 4+ years as a software engineer, with production systems you’ve built and supported.

  • High ownership tendencies

  • Experience in a product-focused organisation, working cross-functionally.

  • Comfortable across multiple languages. We mainly use Kotlin, Java, Python and TypeScript.

  • Able to reason about trade-offs - throughput, latency, consistency, cost - and explain them.

  • At home in system design and in low-level implementation detail.

  • Experience building and deploying services on AWS or GCP.

  • Hands-on exposure to Kafka, Flink, Redis or clustered Postgres, and an appetite for more.

  • Comfortable with agent-based development tools. We use Claude Code; any equivalent is fine.

  • A clear communicator and a pragmatic problem-solver.


NICE TO HAVE EXPERIENCE:

  • Data-intensive applications at scale.

  • Building and interpreting observability - metrics, logging, tracing.

  • Working within or alongside DevOps, SRE or infrastructure teams.

  • Complex distributed environments - high throughput, low latency, large datasets.

  • Any exposure to commodities, energy or financial markets. Useful, but we’ll teach you the domain.

Why Join Sparta?

At Sparta, our culture is built on innovation, collaboration, and high performance. We thrive in a fast-paced environment where initiative is celebrated, challenges are embraced, and impact is rewarded.

• Equity in a high-growth, VC-backed company

• $42M in Series B funding — strong market traction and investment

• Early-stage growth — build your career as we scale

• Market-leading product — we are redefining commodity trading intelligence

• Top-tier tools and technology to support your success

What's the Culture Like at Sparta?

At Sparta, our culture isn't just a set of values on a wall — it's how we work. We embrace a dynamic environment where initiative is celebrated, challenges are met head-on, and innovation thrives. You'll collaborate with people who are passionate about our mission and committed to building outstanding products and outcomes for our customers.

The Sparta Code

Understanding is non-negotiable

Understanding leads to believing. Believing leads to winning.

The 'why' is the difference between compliance and conviction. Before we execute, we ask: why does this matter, who does it serve, what changes if we win? People who understand the mission don't need to be managed.

Ask for forgiveness, not for permission

Most decisions are reversible. Most fears are not.

90% of decisions are reversible. Make them, ship, iterate. Perfection is the enemy of efficiency. Bias for action means moving before you have all the answers, but it isn't recklessness. The rule: tell the rest of us what you did, what changed, what you learned.

Fall in love with the problem

The mission wins. Your idea doesn't have to.

Solutions flatter our ego. They feel like progress. But solutions without problems are opinions, and opinions don't move customers, markets, or teammates. The goal is to find what's true, not to win the room. If your idea gets killed because a better one comes along, that's the system working.

It's your fault. Lucky you.

If it's on you, it's in your control.

True ownership sounds harsh until you feel how liberating it is. If every problem is yours, you stop spending energy on who to blame and start spending it on how to fix it. Effective leaders default to 'it's on me'. Not out of guilt, but out of agency.

Conflict is a gift

Honesty is an expression of care.

Withholding feedback is choosing comfort over growth, yours and your colleague's. Staying silent deprives others of the chance to learn. We challenge openly and with positive intent. Done with care, this builds trust. Done with ego, it destroys it.

Sparta Commodities is proud to be an equal opportunity employer and promotes diversity within its workforce. We are determined that no-one will ever receive less favourable treatment on the grounds of gender, age, disability, religion, belief, sexual orientation, marital status, race, veteran status or any basis covered by appropriate law.

  • Improve observability, monitoring and alerting in Datadog, so problems surface before a trader notices.

  • Take part in incident response, then close the loop on the root cause.

  • Work with our runtime across Lambda, ECS and EKS, and help move more workloads onto Kubernetes.

  • Help operate the data and streaming infrastructure you depend on: Kafka, Flink, Redis/Valkey, RDS, Redshift.

  • Extend our infrastructure as code in AWS CDK, and our CI/CD pipelines.

  • Reduce toil. Automate the manual, delete the unnecessary, make the next incident less likely.

  • High ownership tendencies.

  • Genuine interest in both halves of this role. You want to write the service and own how it runs.

  • Strong in at least one of Kotlin, Java, Python or TypeScript.

  • A solid working understanding of AWS - compute, networking, storage, IAM - from running things in production.

  • Hands-on with infrastructure as code: AWS CDK, Terraform, CloudFormation or similar.

  • Practical experience running container workloads on Kubernetes: deploying, debugging, tuning.

  • Experience with CI/CD tooling and a clear view of a good delivery lifecycle.

  • A habit of instrumenting what you build - metrics, logging, tracing.

  • Experience being on the hook for production, incident response included, and calm when things are on fire.

  • Experience defining or working to service-level objectives, or a clear sense of how you’d start.

  • A strong urge to own and improve things - to spot what isn’t working and fix it.

  • Comfortable with agent-based development tools. We use Claude Code; any equivalent is fine.

  • A clear communicator and a pragmatic problem-solver.


NICE TO HAVE EXPERIENCE:

  • Building or operating a platform on Kubernetes, EKS especially.

  • Datadog specifically.

  • Data or streaming systems: Kafka, Flink, Redshift, clustered Postgres.

  • Working to error budgets, and using them to make real prioritisation calls.

  • Security and compliance best practice in cloud environments.

The Role

Location: London or Geneva. In-office, with flexibility for 1–2 days per week from home.

Reporting to the CEO and managing a team of 3 in People, you'll be Sparta's most senior People leader. Working directly with the CEO and leadership team, you'll define and execute the people strategy required to scale the organisation, ensuring we have the leadership, capability, culture and organisational structure necessary to achieve our long-term growth ambitions.

We're looking for someone with the strategic ability to grow into a CPO role as Sparta scales.

You'll be shaping and scaling the People organisation, building the structure, capability and leadership needed to support Sparta's next phase of growth: compensation and levelling, performance, leadership development, hiring and organisation design, while ensuring the overall People strategy remains aligned to business objectives. Much of what this role owns needs to be improved, perfected or redesigned, so you'll be hands-on from day one, building frameworks and running processes personally before you're managing others through them. You'll be central to building a consistent, high-performance culture across our distributed teams globally.

What You'll Be Doing

  • Develop and execute Sparta's global people strategy, ensuring organisational structure, capability, culture and talent are aligned to support the company's growth from Series B through its next stage of scale, whilst balancing local employment, cultural and regulatory considerations

  • Act as a strategic advisor to the CEO, Executive Team and Board on organisational design, leadership capability, succession planning, workforce risks and culture

  • Build our compensation architecture: salary bands, a levelling framework, and a consistent, transparent approach to pay across geographies.

  • Introduce a structured performance process and individual scorecards, so everyone knows what success looks like for them.

  • Build our leadership pipeline through talent reviews, succession planning and management development. Give managers the confidence and authority to make more decisions themselves and address people problems early.

  • Lead organisation design, ensuring Sparta's operating model, spans and layers, leadership structure and workforce planning evolve appropriately as the business scales internationally. Partner with Finance and functional leaders to develop workforce planning and capability strategies that support Sparta's growth objectives

  • Own talent acquisition strategy and delivery. Work with Marketing and the TA team to grow our employer brand so more great people come to us.

  • Own Learning & Development: coaching, training, and levelling up managers and individual contributors

  • Provide executive oversight of workplace and employee experience across all locations. Partner closely with the Executive Team and other leaders to align hiring philosophy, location strategy, and expectations across Sparta's distributed teams

  • Represent People at the leadership table. Raise risks early and make sure stakeholders always know where things stand

What Success Looks Like in Your First Year

  • Executive Team aligned around a clear people strategy

  • Leadership effectiveness and manager capability measurably improved

  • Workforce plan linked to business objectives

  • Salary bands and a levelling framework live

  • Individual scorecards in place, so everyone knows what success looks like for them

  • A structured performance review running company-wide, with buy-in from key stakeholders

  • A middle-management empowerment programme in place, with managers visibly making more decisions without escalating to the exec team

  • Succession plans in place for key roles

  • Hiring on track against plan, with quality and retention holding up

About You

  • You've been the most senior People leader in a scaling organisation, or held a Director or VP People role with significant strategic accountability

  • You've worked in a Series B–D SaaS or tech scaleup and know the people challenges of that stage first-hand

  • You've personally built compensation, levelling and performance frameworks, and you can point to what you built and the impact it had

  • You can influence founders, boards and senior executives, and challenge constructively when it's needed

  • You're commercially minded. You find workable compromises and build frameworks that fix problems for good

  • You've led organisational change across distributed, multi-country teams, not just rolled out HR programmes. Sparta has people across London, Geneva, Spain, Singapore, Houston, and Dubai - familiarity with local laws, regulations and cultures in these locations is a distinct advantage

  • You take ownership, move with urgency and are comfortable being hands-on

  • You communicate clearly and proactively

  • You want to grow this role into a CPO seat

  • Experience scaling a tech business from around 100 to 300+ people is a big plus

We care more about what you've achieved, and how relevant it is to our stage, than about a specific number of years' experience.

raw.title: Account Executive - Commercial, Spotify Technology
raw.description:
Spotify Technology is our business-to-business software team, helping organizations improve how they build and deliver software. Our products, including Backstage Portal, Confidence, and Xirp, support developers and AI-powered systems as they navigate increasingly complex engineering environments.

As an Account Executive on our Commercial team, you will drive new business for Spotify Technology. You'll focus on companies with fewer than 1,000 employees, where sales cycles typically run from weeks to a few months and success depends on a repeatable, scalable sales motion. You'll manage a high volume of opportunities, work with one or a small group of decision-makers (often a hands-on engineering leader or CTO), and move deals efficiently from the first conversation to close. You'll also help shape the playbook that enables our commercial business to grow.

You'll collaborate with Sales Engineering, Marketing, Product, and Customer Success to create a seamless customer experience. Your ability to quickly understand customers' technical needs and connect them to clear business value will be key to your success.


What You'll Do

• Identify and pursue new business opportunities with companies of fewer than 1,000 employees. While significant inbound demand supports the pipeline, top performers will exceed targets by treating this as a “Hunter” role in addition to converting inbound demand.

• Own the full sales cycle, from prospecting and discovery through demos, proposals, negotiations, and close.

• Manage a high-velocity pipeline across multiple opportunities, keeping deals moving with clear next steps and maintaining accurate pipeline and forecast data in the CRM.

• Achieve and exceed quarterly and annual revenue targets.

• Run efficient, repeatable sales processes and contribute to playbooks that help scale our commercial sales motion.

• Partner with Marketing on inbound and outbound pipeline generation, responding quickly to leads and identifying new opportunities.

• Articulate how Backstage Portal and Confidence solve developer experience challenges, including how AI is reshaping software development.

• Tell a compelling story about Spotify's internal approach to solving engineering challenges and how our products are proven internally at scale.

• Present case studies and customer success stories that demonstrate the impact and business value of our products.

• Partner with Sales Engineering on technical evaluations and ensure a smooth handoff to Customer Success to support onboarding, retention, and expansion.

• Share customer feedback with Product and internal teams to help shape the roadmap.

raw.description:
We are looking for a Data Scientist to join the Business Analytics team within Spotify’s Business Strategy and Insights organization. Our team tackles some of Spotify’s most consequential strategic questions, shaping the trajectory of our business and improving the experiences of our over 700M active users across more than 180 countries.
 
In this role, you will use data analysis, experimentation, and statistical modeling to identify, assess, and launch a broad range of new initiatives and product features that span both product and business teams. You will also regularly assess the health of our business and identify areas of opportunity, translating these insights into clear, actionable recommendations for senior leadership.
 
At Spotify, you'll have access to some of the richest datasets in the world and the autonomy to explore them creatively and rigorously. Above all, your work will shape how the world listens, discovers, and connects through audio.

What You'll Do
  • Develop data-driven strategies to support the growth of Spotify’s active users and subscribers 
  • Create and communicate impactful findings and recommendations that improve the Premium product
  • Model and forecast the impact of new business initiatives
  • Work closely with business partners to understand the changes they are driving and help them discover new opportunities for growth
  • Analyze experiments (A/B tests; quasi-experiments) to measure the impact of new features and go-to-market initiatives
  • Present your findings to senior leaders, influencing the course of our business

    • Who You Are
  • You have 5+ years of professional experience in data science or analytics, ideally at a consumer tech company or top-tier consulting firm.
  • You are fluent in SQL and Python or R, and have a strong grasp of statistical methods and causal inference. Direct experience with product analytics or experimentation is a plus.
  • You enjoy partnering with a range of cross-functional stakeholders and working on varied projects involving different products and problem spaces.
  • You have a strategic mindset and an eye for cleanly extracting the “so what” from complex, technical analyses.

raw.title: Data Scientist, Company Planning & Execution
raw.description:
How does a company with thousands of people building hundreds of products stay focused on what matters most? That's the question the Company Planning and Execution (CPE) team works on every day. We design the systems, processes, and insights that help Spotify plan, prioritise, and deliver at scale.

As a Data Scientist on CPE, you'll sit at the intersection of data, strategy, and operations. You'll bring clarity to complex questions by turning operational and strategic information into clear stories, recommendations, and decision frameworks that help leaders and teams act faster and smarter. You'll also explore how AI and automation can change the way people access insights and make decisions.

You'll work closely with data scientists, engineers, PMs, and business partners across the company to help refine how Spotify executes at scale. If you like making sense of ambiguity, care about how organisations work, and want your analysis to shape real decisions, this is the role.


What You'll Do
  • Formulate hypotheses related to how Spotify plans and delivers, and communicate insights effectively to a range of audiences.
  • Apply analytical techniques — including statistical models and machine learning — to identify trends and generate insights that improve how we work.
  • Build and maintain the data models, pipelines, and dashboards that provide visibility into how Spotify plans and executes.
  • Develop structured narratives and recommendations — not just charts, but the "why" and "so what" — in our semi-annual Planning and Execution Insight reports and recurring briefings.
  • Explore how AI and automation can make insights faster to produce and easier to access across the company.

    • Who You Are
  • Curious about how organisations work — not just the data, but the decisions and systems behind it.
  • 5+ years of experience with a quantitative background in science, economics, engineering, or a related field.
  • Strong interpersonal skills and comfortable working with multiple stakeholders across levels and functions.
  • Able to take messy, complex datasets and turn them into clear recommendations and stories that land with non-technical audiences.
  • Proficient in SQL and Python, comfortable in BigQuery, and experienced with tools like dbt, Tableau, or Looker.
  • Experience with operational or work management data is a plus.

raw.title: Machine Learning Engineer - Subscriptions
raw.description:
At Spotify, our Subscriptions Mission focuses on creating experiences that help listeners discover the value of Spotify, become subscribers, and stay with us for the long term. By combining technology, experimentation, and a deep understanding of our users, we help connect artists and fans while building a sustainable subscription business.

Within the Subscriptions Mission, the Subs Foundational Models Product Area is part of the Subs User Understanding Studio. We build scalable machine learning solutions that personalize the subscriber journey, from conversion through to long-term retention. Working closely with teams across the mission, we develop ML solutions that improve key business metrics, including subscriber growth, monthly active users, and Premium retention.

We're looking for a Machine Learning Engineer to join our Radius squad. You'll take ownership of impactful ML initiatives, develop and improve production models, and contribute to the foundational ML capabilities that power personalization and optimization across Subscriptions.

Your work could include reducing friction for Free users while balancing retention and conversion, improving payment experiences to reduce Premium churn, or developing reusable models such as subscriber embeddings that support multiple products and use cases.


What You'll Do
  • Lead multi-week ML initiatives end to end, from translating business requirements into technical specifications to shipping models and measuring their impact on subscriber metrics
  • Own components of our ML systems, making independent technical trade-offs and keeping them observable, reliable, and well documented
  • Collaborate with a multi-functional agile team spanning user research, design, data science, product management, and engineering to build new product features that advance our mission to connect artists and fans in personalised and relevant ways
  • Prototype new approaches and productionise solutions at scale for our hundreds of millions of active users
  • Help drive optimisation, testing, and tooling to improve quality
  • Unblock and share context with your teammates to raise the whole squad's velocity
  • Use AI-assisted engineering to move faster and remove repetitive toil, while owning the quality of everything you ship
  • Partner closely with senior and staff ML engineers, and be part of an active group of machine learning practitioners in your mission and across Spotify

    • Who You Are
  • You have experience building and shipping production ML systems
  • You have a strong background in machine learning, theory, and practice
  • You are comfortable explaining the intuition and assumptions behind ML concepts
  • You can own well-scoped ML projects end to end and make sound technical decisions independently
  • You communicate clearly with stakeholders and can explain the reasoning behind your technical choices
  • You are curious, open to feedback, and keen to grow your scope over time
  • You have hands-on experience implementing and maintaining production ML systems in Python, Scala, or similar languages, including model development with PyTorch
  • You are experienced with building data pipelines, and you are self-sufficient in getting the data you need to build and evaluate your models
  • You preferably have experience with cloud platforms like GCP or AWS
  • You care about agile software processes, data development, reliability, and focused experimentation
  • You have a desire to drive business impact

    • Where You'll Be

    • We offer you the flexibility to work where you work best! For this role, you can be within the EMEA region as long as we have a work location

raw.title: Principal Product Manager - Core Experience Platform
raw.description:
We design Spotify’s consumer experience—end to end, moment to moment, across every screen, platform, and partner integration. Our mission is to make listening feel effortless, personal, and joyful for billions of users around the world. That means turning complexity into clarity across hundreds of touchpoints—from our mobile and desktop apps to the smart speakers, TVs, cars, and integrations where Spotify shows up every day. If it touches a consumer, we shape it. We bring deep insight into human behavior, design, and technology to craft experiences that feel intuitive, expressive, and unmistakably Spotify.

The Core Experience team builds the foundations that make Spotify feel connected, intuitive, and consistent wherever people listen. From Playlists to shared product capabilities, we help teams across Spotify create experiences that millions of listeners use every day.

We're looking for a Principal Product Manager to shape the future of these platforms. You'll set product direction, bring teams together around shared priorities, and help create the capabilities that make great listening experiences possible at scale. This is an opportunity to influence how Spotify's products evolve while making a meaningful impact on listeners and creators around the world.


What You’ll Do
  • Partner with engineering leaders to explore technical solutions, evaluate trade-offs, and guide decisions that improve product performance, reliability, and scalability.
  • Develop shared platform capabilities that help teams build consistent, high-quality experiences across Spotify.
  • Improve the adoption and long-term value of platform capabilities by gathering feedback, measuring outcomes, and supporting teams that use them.
  • Balance new product opportunities with technical improvements, including system performance, quality, simplification, and platform migrations.
  • Use experimentation, prototypes, technical exploration, and feedback to test ideas, learn quickly, and adapt your approach.
  • Build alignment across teams by communicating priorities, dependencies, and trade-offs clearly, helping partners work toward shared outcomes.

    • Who You Are
  • You have 5+ years of product management experience, including experience building or improving technical platforms, shared systems, or capabilities that support consumer products.
  • You understand client and backend technologies and can work with engineers to connect technical decisions to user needs and business outcomes.
  • You're familiar with mobile development for iOS or Android, including areas such as app performance, reliability, user interface architecture, or design systems.
  • You have experience guiding products or platforms beyond launch, improving adoption, managing technical debt, and supporting systems as needs evolve.
  • You can evaluate technical trade-offs and make thoughtful decisions about when to improve existing systems, simplify solutions, or invest in new capabilities.
  • You use data, research, experimentation, and sound judgment to make product decisions, including when traditional A/B testing isn't the right approach.
  • You communicate complex ideas clearly, welcome different perspectives, and build strong relationships across engineering, design, and data teams.

raw.title: Product Manager - Customer Service Platform
raw.description:
The Subscriptions Mission builds and evolves Spotify’s subscription products and marketplace experiences to drive sustainable user and revenue growth globally. We focus on awareness, acquisition, activation, retention, and monetization strategies that help users unlock the full value of Spotify while enabling the business to scale efficiently and responsibly.

Spotify's Customer Service Platform powers interactions between our users and support teams. As a Product Manager, you will shape the tools, channels, and foundational APIs that enable our advisors to deliver fast, effective, and empathetic support at scale.

You’ll help improve the advisor experience through intelligent tooling, define how customers reach support across channels, and strengthen the API layer underpinning our service ecosystem. Your work will bring platform thinking together with real human impact, helping our advisors do their best work and improving how users experience Spotify support.

 

What You'll Do
  • Own the product vision and roadmap for the tools our support advisors use every day, improving efficiency and enabling better outcomes for users.
  • Define and evolve how customers access support across chat, email, social messaging, and emerging channels, helping the right contact reach the right advisor at the right time.
  • Strengthen the foundational API layer connecting our support systems, with a focus on reliability, extensibility, and developer experience as the platform scales.
  • Take initiatives from discovery through launch, partnering closely with engineering to ship iteratively, learn quickly, and deliver meaningful outcomes.
  • Identify opportunities to thoughtfully apply AI and automation within advisor workflows and channel routing to improve speed, accuracy, and the advisor experience.
  • Collaborate with engineering, design, data science, and customer service operations to build scalable capabilities that serve both advisors and users.
  • Define meaningful success metrics, run experiments, and use data and customer insights to make clear prioritisation decisions and measure impact.

Who You Are
  • You have 4+ years of product management experience and a track record of delivering impactful products in technology-driven environments.
  • You think in systems and understand how APIs, integrations, platforms, and tooling can work together to create leverage across an organisation.
  • You are comfortable partnering with engineering teams on API design, system architecture, and technical trade-offs; you don't need to write code, but you can engage confidently in technical conversations.
  • You know how to take products from discovery through delivery, balancing thoughtful product development with the pace needed to learn and make progress.
  • You are curious about customer service and support operations and bring empathy for both the people providing support and the users receiving it.
  • You communicate clearly, can make complex trade-offs understandable, and know how to create alignment across technical and non-technical partners.
  • You use data, experimentation, customer insight, and judgement to make decisions and are comfortable adapting when you learn something new.
  • You enjoy working collaboratively across disciplines and care about building products that create meaningful outcomes for customers and the people who support them.

raw.title: Product Manager - Data Platform
raw.description:
Spotify’s mission is to unlock the potential of human creativity by giving a million creative artists the opportunity to live off their art and billions of fans the chance to enjoy and be passionate about these creators.

Data is a means to an end, and Spotify extracts value from data through application. The Data Platform Studio helps Spotify win by enabling the application of data in an intuitive and efficient way.

Data Platform is responsible for how data is collected, processed, stored, governed, and made available to the thousands of engineers, data scientists, analysts, and machine learning practitioners who build Spotify’s products. As AI agents increasingly generate code, write data pipelines, and power personalized user experiences, Data Platform sits at the center of one of the most important infrastructure domains at Spotify.

We're looking for a passionate Product Manager to join the team responsible for Spotify’s data catalogue, metadata, and data lineage capabilities. In this role, you'll own the strategy and roadmap for a critical part of Spotify's data ecosystem, helping users discover, understand, trust, and safely use data at scale. You'll work closely with engineers, designers, data scientists, and product teams across Spotify to make working with data faster, safer, and more intuitive.


What You'll Do
  • Develop and own the product strategy and roadmap for Spotify's data catalogue, metadata, and data lineage domain.
  • Diagnose and deeply understand the needs of Spotify's data community, including data engineers, data scientists, analysts, ML engineers, and increasingly AI agents.
  • Identify and prioritize the highest-impact problems to solve, balancing user needs, business priorities, platform requirements, and regulatory considerations.
  • Evaluate and deliver solutions through building, buying, or integrating third-party products and capabilities.
  • Define success metrics and KPIs that measure adoption, value creation, and business impact.
  • Build strong relationships with internal product, engineering, analytics, and data teams to understand workflows, gather feedback, and shape future platform investments.
  • Collaborate closely with engineering, design, and data science partners to deliver high-quality platform experiences.
  • Influence stakeholders across the Data Platform Studio and broader Spotify organization to align around product direction and priorities.
  • Help shape how Spotify approaches metadata, governance, discoverability, lineage, and trust in an increasingly AI-driven world.
  • Stay informed on industry trends across data platforms, developer tools, AI/ML infrastructure, analytics, and data governance.

    • Who You Are
  • You have 2+ years of Product Management experience, ideally working on platform products, developer tools, data infrastructure, analytics platforms, or data governance systems.
  • You have a technical foundation through a degree in Computer Science, Engineering, a related field, and/or prior experience in engineering or technical roles.
  • You are comfortable working with engineers and can engage in technical discussions while representing customer and business needs.
  • You are an excellent communicator and collaborator who can build alignment across teams with different priorities and levels of technical expertise.
  • You have strong systems-thinking skills and can connect workflows, platforms, users, and business outcomes.
  • You have empathy for people who work with data and understand the challenges they face every day.

raw.title: Senior Backend Engineer - Content Platform
raw.description:
We design Spotify’s consumer experience—end to end, moment to moment, across every screen, platform, and partner integration. Our mission is to make listening feel effortless, personal, and joyful for billions of users around the world. That means turning complexity into clarity across hundreds of touchpoints—from our mobile and desktop apps to the smart speakers, TVs, cars, and integrations where Spotify shows up every day. If it touches a consumer, we shape it. We bring deep insight into human behavior, design, and technology to craft experiences that feel intuitive, expressive, and unmistakably Spotify.

We own music content ingestion at Spotify, which is how music from labels, distributors and other partners gets onto the platform. We receive industry-standard deliveries, validate them, and turn them into the catalog data that teams across Spotify build on, including lyrics, rights and supply data. As we add new content types and partners, we’re building an ingestion platform that scales without a custom build every time.


What You'll Do
  • Build and run the backend services and data pipelines that ingest, validate and process music deliveries from partners, covering audio, metadata, lyrics and new content types
  • Own large parts of the ingestion pipeline and lead technical work as we add video, richer partner data and other new content
  • Make ingestion more reliable, catch data quality problems at the point of entry, and improve the operational tooling around the pipeline
  • Design and evolve APIs and schemas that other teams depend on, keeping contracts stable and backward compatible
  • Help move validation towards real time and make Silk Road a well-documented, self-serve platform
  • Deliver roadmap work, take part in planning, review code, and share on-call
  • Work with Content Ops, operations tooling teams, partner teams and the product teams that build on our content

    • Who You Are
  • You have strong experience building and operating backend services and data pipelines in production at scale, ideally in Java, Scala or Go
  • You have designed APIs and handled schema evolution and backward compatibility in systems where other teams rely on stable contracts
  • You’re comfortable modelling data for auditability, versioning and efficient querying and  understand the tradeoffs between real-time and batch processing
  • You lead projects from discovery to handover, make sound technical decisions, and mentor others
  • You may have worked with content ingestion, metadata standards such as DDEX, B2B partner integrations, rights or compliance-sensitive data, lyrics or time-synced data, or GCP.

    • Where You'll Be
  • This role is based in London or Stockholm.
  • We offer you the flexibility to work where you work best! There will be some in person meetings, but still allows for flexibility to work from home.

raw.title: Staff Product Designer - Platform Design
raw.description:
The Platform team creates the technology that enables Spotify to learn quickly and scale easily, enabling rapid growth in our users and our business around the globe. Spanning many disciplines, we work to make the business work; creating the infrastructure, tooling, frameworks, and capabilities needed to welcome a billion customers.

Spotify runs on the tools we've built for ourselves. They help hundreds of teams ship every day to hundreds of millions of people around the world. Now, we're sharing them.

Spotify Technology brings our proven tools and services together for engineering organisations everywhere, from global enterprises to individual developers. As AI reshapes how software gets made, we're building on years of experience solving complex engineering challenges at scale.

Platform Design makes these powerful tools feel effortless. We shape the services, products and experiences used by Spotify's engineering teams and by developers around the world. We believe great design is a competitive advantage, and developer tools deserve the same care and craft as any consumer product.

As a Staff Product Designer, you'll combine product leadership with hands-on design and engineering. You'll shape the experience strategy for a key part of the Spotify Technology portfolio, establish a distinctive visual language, and turn internal tools into products customers love using. You'll work closely with product, engineering and marketing partners, reporting to the Spotify Technology Design Director.


What You'll Do
  • Lead complex design challenges from early exploration through to production, creating intuitive flows, interfaces, interactions and motion that make powerful developer tools easier to use.
  • Shape the visual language of Spotify Technology, bringing consistency, personality and craft across product experiences and brand touchpoints.
  • Transform tools built for Spotify's engineering teams into compelling commercial products that meet the needs of developers and enterprise customers.
  • Bring design to life in code, building and shipping high-quality front-end experiences with close attention to performance, accessibility and detail.
  • Set experience strategy across your product area, partnering with product and engineering leaders to influence priorities, guide decisions and shape the roadmap.
  • Use prototypes, storytelling and experimentation to make complex ideas tangible, build alignment and help teams navigate trade-offs.
  • Explore how generative AI and agentic tools can improve design and development workflows, while creating thoughtful experiences for products used by people and AI agents.
  • Raise the bar for design craft across the team, championing design systems, inclusive experiences and a culture of collaboration, feedback and continuous learning.

    •  


Who You Are
  • You have a strong background in product design, with experience shaping complex digital products and delivering high-quality visual and interaction design.
  • You're comfortable working across strategy and execution, setting a clear product direction while staying close to the details of design and delivery.
  • You can build and ship user interfaces using a modern front-end technology stack, and enjoy bringing your designs into production.
  • You understand how to create cohesive visual experiences across product and brand, with a thoughtful approach to interaction, motion and design systems.
  • You bring an understanding of developer tools, enterprise software or platform products, including the challenges of designing for technical audiences.
  • You use generative AI and agentic tools in your work, applying sound judgement about where they add value and where human expertise matters most.
  • You're comfortable navigating ambiguity, using research, data and customer insights to make informed decisions and solve complex problems.
  • You communicate ideas clearly, build trust across disciplines and influence product decisions through compelling design work and storytelling.
  • You care about helping others grow, welcome different perspectives and contribute to an inclusive, collaborative environment where great work can happen.

Where You'll Be
  • This role is based in London, UK or Stockholm, Sweden
  • We offer you the flexibility to work where you work best! There will be some in person meetings, but still allows for flexibility to work from home.

raw.title: Senior Databricks Data Engineer
raw.description:
Role Summary

We are looking for a Senior Databricks Data Engineer with proven hands-on Databricks experience to build, develop and manage STACK’s enterprise data platform. This is a production-focused engineering role requiring practical expertise in Databricks, PySpark, Python, SQL and Delta Lake.

The role will design reliable pipelines integrating Finance, Delivery, Operations, HR and PMO systems, establish governed and high-quality datasets, and support secure, scalable analytics and reporting. Working with technical and business stakeholders, the successful candidate will take ownership of data engineering solutions and help improve the reliability and performance of the platform.

Key Responsibilities:

· Design, develop, deploy and maintain production-grade ETL/ELT pipelines using Databricks, PySpark, Python and SQL, integrating APIs, databases, SaaS applications, files and spreadsheets.

· Develop and optimize scalable Delta Lake data models and lakehouse architecture for reporting, analytics and future AI use cases.

· Build, schedule, monitor and troubleshoot data processing jobs using Databricks Workflows, Lakeflow or Delta Live Tables, as appropriate.

· Apply Unity Catalog governance, including access permissions, data ownership, lineage and common data definitions.

· Support Databricks workspaces, compute resources, SQL Warehouses, service principals and access management in partnership with relevant technology teams.

· Manage development, test and production deployments, monitoring, incident resolution and recovery, using Git and CI/CD practices.

· Optimise pipeline performance, Spark processing, compute usage and platform costs while maintaining appropriate security and operational controls.

· Implement data quality checks for completeness, accuracy, timeliness, consistency, duplicates and reconciliation with source systems.

· Build monitoring and alerting to identify pipeline failures, data quality issues and operational risks.

· Integrate reliable, governed Databricks datasets with Power BI and other approved analytical tools.

· Work with Finance, Delivery, Operations, HR and PMO teams to translate requirements into sustainable data solutions.

· Document pipelines, dependencies, controls and operating procedures, and coordinate specialist external partners when required.

Qualifications:

  • Own the day-to-day relationship for a portfolio of Key Accounts, building trusted partnerships with stakeholders across research, insights and strategy functions and deepening toward senior and executive contacts as the relationship matures, working in partnership with a Key Account Manager (KAM), and being the person clients call when they want to get more from the platform

offer.title: Member of Scientific Staff, Cell Culture and Functional Assays

raw.title: Member of Scientific Staff, Cell Culture and Functional Assays
raw.description:
LOCATION: King's Cross, London · PATTERN: Lab-based, full-time

The opportunity

We're a stealth startup in AI and bio, building infrastructure for data generation. The team is small and elite, the problems are hard, and the foundations are being laid right now. You'd help write them from the first line, with real ownership and a direct line to the founders.

This role covers the cell side of our protein characterisation work. You would keep the cell lines healthy and run the assays that show how a designed protein behaves on a living cell, week after week, to the same standard.

About us

AI for biology has a data problem. The data that matters most doesn't exist yet, so we're building the infrastructure to produce it, with quality and traceability built in from day one.

We're in stealth and heads-down on execution. We'll share more about what we're building once you've spoken with the team.

The role

You will run cell culture and the cell-based assays for our protein characterisation work. That means the mammalian lines the assays depend on, from thaw through routine passage to a banked and documented stock, and the weekly rhythm of seeding, treating, reading and reporting plates.

Most of it runs in 384-well plates with imaging-based or flow cytometry readouts. You will run those assays as designed, with the controls and replicates that make a curve defensible, and you will be the person who notices when a plate, a line or a reagent lot has started to drift.

Assay design and the shape of the cascade sit with the scientist who leads this work today, so you are not being asked to invent the panel. You are being asked to make it run the same way every week, to record what you did in a form the rest of the system can read, and to tighten the protocols as they settle, including moving them towards the plate formats our automation will take on.

Your first 90 days

FIRST 30 DAYS

◆ Take over routine culture and banking for the protein cell lines, working to the protocols we already run.

◆ Learn the panel end to end by running each assay alongside the scientist who owns it.

DAYS 30 TO 60

◆ Run at least one assay in the panel independently, including its controls and acceptance criteria.

◆ Revise one culture or assay protocol so that someone else could follow it without asking you.

DAYS 60 TO 90

◆ Hold the weekly assay schedule on your own and return results on the agreed turnaround.

◆ Bring one protocol to a tighter precision bar, or into a plate format ready for automation.

Who you are

You are a hands-on cell biologist who takes assay variability personally. You have run the same assay often enough to tell a real effect from a bad plate, and you would rather find the cause than repeat the run.

The week has a rhythm in this job: cells to feed, plates to seed, runs to finish, numbers to return. You are happy with that, you keep records someone else can pick up, and you say early when something looks wrong rather than at the end of the week.

We do not hire people into boxes. The team is small, and early hires here end up owning work beyond the job they joined for. Nobody arrives with every part of this role. If you are strong in most of it and quick to learn the rest, we want to hear from you.

MUST HAVE

◆ Strong hands-on mammalian cell culture: adherent and suspension lines, aseptic technique, and thawing, passaging and banking to a high and consistent standard.

◆ Experience running cell-based assays end to end, including relevant controls, replicates and dose-response curves behind a reported number.

◆ Comfort with plate-based work and the arithmetic that goes with it, such as dilution series, plate maps and normalisation.

◆ Careful, traceable record-keeping that someone else can follow without asking you.

◆ A PhD in cell biology, pharmacology, immunology or a related field, or an MSc and two to three years of relevant lab experience.

NICE TO HAVE

◆ Reporter cell line bioassays for binding or blockade.

◆ Receptor internalisation, lysosomal trafficking or cytotoxicity assays.

◆ High-content or fluorescence imaging, and the image analysis behind it.

◆ 384-well formats, liquid handlers or other plate-based automation.

◆ Flow cytometry, for example for surface receptor quantification.

Why this is unusual

Most cell-based assay roles sit inside a discovery project. You build an assay, you answer a question with it, and the assay goes quiet. This one is closer to running an instrument. The same assays run every week against a stream of new molecules, and the number that comes out is the product.

That changes what good looks like. Precision matters more than novelty, a protocol is only finished when someone else can run it and get your answer, and every passage, plate and reagent lot is captured as structured data, because a result is only as trustworthy as the cells behind it.

Some people find that energising; some find it outside their lane. Worth knowing in advance which one you are.

How we work

This is a lab-based role at our site in King's Cross, London. The cells are in the lab, so most of your week will be too, with room for writing and analysis away from the bench. The wider team is distributed and travels, so you will work with people who are not always in the building.

We work in the open. Decisions are written down, work happens centrally rather than scattered across tools, and the week opens with a session the whole company attends. There is a quarterly offsite. Each person owns their area and makes the call inside it, and we will expect that of you early rather than late.

UK benefits are 30 days of annual leave plus public holidays, a pension with a 10% employer contribution, and top-tier Bupa private health cover. More is added as the team grows.

The team you will join

You will join the protein characterisation team and report to its lead. Day to day you will work with the scientist who designs the assay cascade, with the protein production and molecular characterisation scientists upstream of you, with the functional genomics team who share the cell culture suite, and with the engineers building the software and automation the lab runs on.

We are a small, elite team, and this is the first seat given entirely to the cell-based side of the work.

Our process

Our process has four stages. A short screening call about the role and the practicalities. A behavioural interview about how you work, run from the same template for every candidate, before anything technical. A technical stage with the protein characterisation team, built around real work rather than a puzzle, including time with us in person at the lab. Then references, aimed at whatever we still want to understand.

If you are not sure whether you match every line above, apply anyway. We would rather read it and decide.

We are an equal opportunity employer. We make hiring decisions on merit, scope-fit, and the strength of the working relationship we expect to build with each hire. Applications welcome from candidates of any background.
